It produces air conditioning and heat-pump systems for homes, offices and factories, commercial refrigeration and refrigerant chemicals, and sells them in more than 170 countries.
dal: Delta Air Lines is one of the world's largest airlines, headquartered at its main hub in Atlanta, Georgia, and founded in 1925. It flies passengers and cargo across the US and to hundreds of cities worldwide, belongs to SkyTeam and even owns an oil refinery.
danske: Danske Bank is Denmark's largest bank, based in Copenhagen and founded in 1871. It serves personal, business and corporate customers mainly in Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Norway, and also offers asset management, pensions and investment banking.
dao: DAO Maker is a crypto launchpad and incubator that helps early-stage blockchain startups raise money and find users. Through its token sales, ordinary investors can get allocations in new projects; the DAO token is used for staking and access to these sales.
dar: Darling Ingredients is an American company based in Texas that recycles food and animal by-products into feed, fats, collagen and gelatin. Together with Valero it produces renewable diesel through the Diamond Green Diesel joint venture.
dash: DoorDash is a US food and grocery delivery platform based in San Francisco, founded in 2013 by Stanford students. Its app connects restaurants and shops with customers and couriers; it also owns Wolt in Europe and has become the largest food delivery service in the United States.
dash-token: Dash is a cryptocurrency for fast, cheap payments, launched in 2014 by Evan Duffield (first as XCoin, then Darkcoin). Its network uses masternodes for instant InstantSend transfers and its own funding and governance system.
data: Data Network (DATA) is a layer-1 blockchain built to register intellectual property rights for data used in AI. It lets owners record rights to datasets on-chain and earn from them, and the DATA token is used inside the network.
data-ru: Arenadata Group is a Russian software developer that builds platforms for storing and processing large volumes of data, such as the Arenadata DB analytical database, for banks, telecoms and industry. It listed on the Moscow Exchange in 2024.
db1: Deutsche Börse is a German exchange group based in Frankfurt. It runs the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and the Xetra trading system, the Eurex derivatives exchange and the Clearstream depository, and calculates the DAX and STOXX indices.
dbk: Deutsche Bank is Germany's largest bank, based in Frankfurt and founded in 1870. It does investment banking, serves corporations and private customers (including through Postbank) and manages assets through DWS.
dbr: deBridge (DBR) is a cross-chain protocol for moving assets and data quickly between blockchains, including Solana and EVM networks, without its own liquidity pools. Its DLN service executes swaps between networks in seconds; DBR is used for governance and rewards.
dbx: Dropbox is a San Francisco cloud storage and collaboration service founded in 2007 by Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi. It lets people and teams store, sync and share files across devices, with tools for e-signatures and document sharing.
dci: Donaldson is an American filter maker based in Minnesota, founded in 1915. It produces air, fuel, oil and hydraulic filters for engines, trucks and construction machines, as well as industrial dust-collection and filtration systems.
dcr: Decred is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 with hybrid consensus: miners create blocks (Proof of Work), while DCR holders who stake their coins validate them and vote on changes. This way the community itself governs the network, and part of new issuance funds its development.
dcty: DacityCoin (DCTY) is a community token on the Solana blockchain that was launched through Pump.fun, the popular platform for creating new Solana tokens. Its price depends mainly on community interest.
dd: DuPont is a US materials company based in Wilmington, Delaware, founded in 1802 by Éleuthère Irénée du Pont as a gunpowder maker. Today it makes specialty materials such as Tyvek, water-filtration and purification systems, and components for healthcare and construction.
ddog: Datadog is a US company based in New York, founded in 2010, that makes a cloud monitoring service. It collects metrics, logs and traces from servers and applications so engineers can see outages and security threats in one place.
de: Deere & Company is a US maker of agricultural and construction machinery based in Illinois, founded in 1837 by John Deere. It is known for its green John Deere tractors and combines and for precision-farming technology.
debit: Teller (DEBIT) is a decentralized lending and borrowing project on BNB Chain. Users can lend crypto to earn interest or take loans against their assets, and DEBIT is the project's token.
deck: Deckers Brands is a US footwear company from Goleta, California. It owns UGG, famous for its sheepskin boots, HOKA, known for thick-soled running shoes, and the sandal brand Teva.
deep: DeepBook (DEEP) is the native decentralized order book of the Sui network, launched in July 2023 with support from Mysten Labs and the Sui Foundation. Exchanges and DeFi apps on Sui use it for trading, and the DEEP token gives fee discounts and voting rights.
defi: De.Fi (DEFI) is the token of De.Fi, a Web3 security and portfolio platform (formerly DeFiYield) with tools such as a smart-contract scanner, the Shield wallet-risk checker, the REKT database of hacks and a multi-chain dashboard.
degen: Degen (DEGEN) is a community token of the Base network that appeared in 2024 among users of the Farcaster social network. It is used to tip content creators and active members, and the project later launched its own Degen Chain.
deli: Delimobil (Carsharing Russia) is Russia's largest car-sharing company, founded in Moscow in 2015. Through its app, users rent cars by the minute, hour or day in Moscow, St Petersburg and other big cities.
dell: Dell Technologies is an American computer maker based in Round Rock, Texas, founded in 1984 by Michael Dell in his college dorm room. It sells Dell, XPS and Alienware laptops and PCs as well as servers, data storage and infrastructure for AI data centers.
delta: Delta Electronics (Thailand) is the Thai subsidiary of Taiwan's Delta Electronics, with factories in Samut Prakan province. It makes power supplies, electric-vehicle components and power equipment for data centres, mostly for export.
delta-electronics: Delta Electronics is a Taiwanese electronics maker based in Taipei, founded by Bruce Cheng in 1971. It is a world leader in power supplies and cooling fans and also builds data-centre power systems, EV chargers and industrial automation.
delta-token: Delta is a DeFi liquidity platform on Robinhood Chain that makes it easier to create, customise and track liquidity-provider positions, with trading fees credited to each provider. It calls itself a tool built by LPs for LPs.
demant: Demant is a Danish hearing health company based near Copenhagen, founded in 1904 by Hans Demant and controlled by the William Demant Foundation. It is one of the world's largest hearing-aid makers through brands such as Oticon, Philips Hearing Solutions and Bernafon, runs hearing clinics and makes audiological diagnostic equipment.
denso: Denso is a Japanese auto parts maker from Kariya, founded in 1949 as a spin-off from Toyota. It makes air conditioning systems, electronics, sensors, spark plugs and components for hybrid and electric cars for carmakers worldwide.
dent: Dent is a mobile-data project from Finland, started in 2017, with an app that sells eSIM data plans and lets users buy, sell and gift mobile data. DENT is the token used for payments and rewards in the app.
deod: Decentrawood is a metaverse platform that combines blockchain, virtual reality and AI to create a virtual world where users can own land, work, socialize and run businesses. DEOD is the token used for payments inside this virtual world.
dep: DEAPCOIN (DEP) is the token of the Japanese gaming platform PlayMining, run by Singapore-based Digital Entertainment Asset. Users earn DEP by playing free games and enjoying manga and anime content, and can use it to buy NFTs.
deso: DeSo (Decentralized Social) is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for social media apps, storing posts, profiles and follows on-chain. It grew out of the BitClout project, and the DESO token pays fees and powers creator coins and tipping.
desu: Dexsport is a Web3 betting and gaming platform that combines sports betting, esports and casino games in one interface. Players sign up with e-mail, Google or Telegram or connect a crypto wallet; DESU is its utility token for rewards, lotteries and the community.
deus: XMAQUINA (DEUS) is a DAO that gives its community shared access to investments in humanoid robotics and physical AI companies, which are usually open only to venture funds. DEUS is the governance token used to vote on the DAO's decisions.
dexe: DeXe (DEXE) is a protocol for creating and running decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). It offers ready-made tools for voting, treasuries and delegation, and the DEXE token is used to govern the platform itself.
dext: DexTools is an analytics app for traders on decentralized exchanges, running since 2020: it shows live charts, new token pairs, liquidity and wallet activity across many blockchains. Holding DEXT unlocks premium features and discounts.
dextf: Memento (DEXTF), formerly DEXTF Protocol, is a DeFi platform for building and trading tokenized crypto portfolios, a decentralized take on exchange-traded funds where one token holds a basket of assets.
dg: Dollar General is an American discount store chain from Tennessee, founded in 1939, with more than 20,000 small stores. It sells food, cleaning supplies, household goods and clothing at low prices, mostly in small towns and rural areas.
dg-fr: Vinci is a French construction and concessions group, one of the largest in the world. It builds roads, bridges and buildings, operates toll motorways in France and airports through Vinci Airports (including London Gatwick), and provides energy infrastructure services.
dg-token: DeGate is a decentralized exchange built as a zero-knowledge rollup on Ethereum, offering an order book with limit orders and grid trading without giving up custody of funds. DG is its governance and utility token.
dgai: DGrid AI (DGAI) is a decentralized AI infrastructure network that gives access to many AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible gateway. The network routes requests between model providers and node operators and settles payments for their services.
dge: Diageo is the world's largest maker of spirits, based in London and formed in 1997. It owns brands such as Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Baileys, Captain Morgan, Tanqueray and Don Julio tequila.
dgld: Digital Gold (DGLD) is a token representing ownership of allocated physical gold stored in a Swiss vault in Castel San Pietro. It is issued by Gold Token SA, the tokenization arm of the precious-metals group MKS PAMP.
dgx: Quest Diagnostics is the largest network of diagnostic laboratories in the US, headquartered in Secaucus, New Jersey. It runs blood tests and other lab tests for doctors, hospitals, employers and patients.
dher: Delivery Hero is a German online food-delivery company based in Berlin, founded in 2011. It runs apps such as foodpanda, Talabat, Glovo and Baemin in dozens of countries across Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America, delivering restaurant meals and groceries.
dhi: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States by number of homes sold, a position it has held since 2002. Based in Arlington, Texas, and founded in 1978 by Donald R. Horton, it builds mostly entry-level and move-up single-family homes in dozens of states under brands such as Express Homes and Emerald Homes.
dhl: DHL Group (formerly Deutsche Post DHL) is a German logistics group based in Bonn. It is the world's largest express delivery and freight operator under the DHL brand and also runs Germany's national postal service, Deutsche Post.
dhr: Danaher is a US science and technology conglomerate from Washington, D.C., founded in 1969 by brothers Steven and Mitchell Rales. It makes diagnostic equipment, biotechnology tools and lab systems under brands such as Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, Leica Biosystems and Cytiva.
dia: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) is an ETF on the Dow Jones index: 30 of the best-known large US companies, weighted by share price.
dia-token: DIA is a cross-chain oracle from Switzerland that delivers asset prices and other data, collected from primary sources, to smart contracts on dozens of blockchains. The DIA token is used for governance and staking.
diam: Diamante (DIAM) is a Layer 1 blockchain built around quantum-resistant security for everyday crypto use. It pairs a proof-of-stake validator set with post-quantum signature schemes and an execution layer that processes transactions in parallel for fast finality.
dias: Diasoft is a Russian software developer founded in 1991 that builds systems for banks and other financial companies. Its products cover core banking, payments, securities and reporting, and are used by many Russian banks.
die: D'Ieteren Group is a Belgian family-controlled investment company based in Brussels, with roots going back to 1805. It distributes Volkswagen Group cars in Belgium and owns most of Belron, the vehicle-glass repair group behind Carglass and Safelite.
diem: DIEM is a token of Venice, a private AI platform, issued on the Base network. Each DIEM gives its holder a daily allowance of Venice API compute for AI models, and new DIEM is created by locking staked VVV tokens.
dime: DIME is the token of Paradex, a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures that runs on its own Starknet-based appchain and was incubated by the crypto investment firm Paradigm. Traders keep custody of their funds while trading with an order book.
dimo: DIMO is an open network that lets drivers connect their cars through an app or a small plug-in device and own and share their vehicle data. Drivers earn DIMO tokens for contributing data, and developers use it to build apps for insurance, maintenance, car sales and more.
dingo: Dingocoin (DINGO) is a community meme coin in the style of Dogecoin, with its own proof-of-work blockchain. It launched in 2021 and is mined with Scrypt, like Dogecoin and Litecoin.
dino: HF Sinclair is a US energy company from Dallas, formed in 2022 when HollyFrontier combined with Sinclair Oil. It runs oil refineries, sells fuel through Sinclair-branded gas stations with the famous green dinosaur, and makes lubricants and renewable diesel.
dis: The Walt Disney Company is an American media and entertainment company based in Burbank, California, founded in 1923 by Walt and Roy Disney. It owns the Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm studios, the Disney+ streaming service, the ABC and ESPN networks, and theme parks around the world.
disco: Disco is a Japanese equipment maker from Tokyo that makes machines for cutting and grinding semiconductor wafers. Its dicing and wafer-thinning tools are used by almost all chipmakers, including for HBM memory.
ditau: DITGOLD (DITAU) is the native token of DitGold, a decentralized ecosystem built on the idea that data is the new gold. The project aims to recognize and tokenize the value of data, giving people transparent ownership of it and a share in the data economy.
divi: Divi is a proof-of-stake cryptocurrency designed to make staking and running masternodes simple for everyday users. Its wallet lets holders earn staking rewards in a few clicks without technical setup.
divislab: Divi's Laboratories is an Indian pharmaceutical company from Hyderabad, founded in 1990 by Murali Divi. It is one of the world's largest makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates, producing them for generic drugmakers and global pharma companies, plus nutraceuticals.
djed: Djed is an overcollateralized stablecoin on Cardano that aims to stay at one US dollar. It was designed with research from IOG and launched by COTI in 2023; each DJED is backed by ADA in a reserve, with the SHEN reserve coin absorbing price swings.
dji6930: DOWGE (DJI6930) is a meme coin that mixes the Dow Jones index with the Doge meme; its ticker is a nod to the SPX6900 meme coin. It has no product of its own: its value rests on community interest and trading.
djt-etf: Trump Media & Technology Group is a US media company from Sarasota, Florida, majority owned by Donald Trump. It runs the social network Truth Social, launched in 2022, the streaming service Truth+ and the investment brand Truth.Fi, and it also holds bitcoin on its balance sheet.
dka: dKargo is a South Korean blockchain project for logistics that links data from carriers, warehouses and delivery services to track shipments transparently. DKA is the token for payments and rewards on the network.
dkng: DraftKings is a US sports betting and online gaming company from Boston, founded in 2012 as a daily fantasy sports site. It runs an online sportsbook and casino in many US states and Canada, the Jackpocket lottery app and fantasy contests.
dks: Dick's Sporting Goods is the largest sporting goods retailer in the US, founded in 1948 by Richard Stack. It sells equipment, footwear and apparel for sports and outdoor activities and also owns the Golf Galaxy chain.
dlb: Dolby Laboratories is a US audio and imaging technology company based in San Francisco, founded by Ray Dolby in London in 1965. It develops Dolby Atmos sound and Dolby Vision picture technologies and licenses them to device makers, streaming services and cinemas.
dlekg: Delek Group is an Israeli energy holding company based in Tel Aviv. Its main assets are control of NewMed Energy, a partner in the Leviathan gas field off Israel, and a large stake in Ithaca Energy, an oil and gas producer in the UK North Sea.
dlf: DLF is one of India's largest real estate developers, founded in 1946 and based in Gurugram near Delhi. It builds luxury housing and owns office parks and shopping malls, including DLF Cyber City and Mall of India, much of it through a rental joint venture.
dlr: Digital Realty is a US company based in Austin, Texas, founded in 2004, and one of the world's largest owners of data centres. It leases space, power and connectivity for servers to cloud providers and corporations in dozens of major cities and is structured as a REIT.
dltr: Dollar Tree is a US discount store chain from Virginia, where most items sell for a single low fixed price of about a dollar. It sells household basics, food, party supplies and stationery in thousands of stores in the US and Canada.
dmart: Avenue Supermarts is an Indian company from Mumbai that runs the DMart hypermarket chain, founded by Radhakishan Damani in 2002. It sells groceries, household goods and clothing at low prices, usually in stores it owns.
dmc: DeLorean (DMC) is the token of DeLorean Labs, the Web3 arm of the DeLorean car brand made famous by the "Back to the Future" films. It is issued on the Sui blockchain and used in the brand's digital and fan community programs.
dmd: Diamond (DMD) is one of the older cryptocurrencies, launched in 2013, which later moved to its own DMD Diamond blockchain with an Ethereum-compatible design and a validator-based consensus. DMD is the native coin used for fees and staking.
dmtr: Dimitra is an agritech platform that gives small farmers digital tools: satellite imagery, soil sensors and machine learning help them plan crops, improve yields and track their produce. DMTR is the token used for payments and governance in the Dimitra ecosystem.
dna: NeoSoul is a project building market infrastructure for the AI-agent economy, where agents learn, compete, coordinate and create measurable value. DNA is the ecosystem token.
dnb: DNB is Norway's largest bank, based in Oslo, with the Norwegian state as its biggest shareholder. It serves personal and corporate customers with banking, mortgages, insurance, pensions and asset management, and is a major lender to the global shipping, energy and seafood industries.
dnp: Dino Polska is a Polish supermarket chain founded in 1999 by Tomasz Biernacki in the Greater Poland region. It runs thousands of mid-sized neighbourhood grocery stores, mostly in small towns and villages, and keeps opening new ones quickly.
dnt: district0x (DNT) is an Ethereum project launched in 2017 for creating decentralized marketplaces and communities, called districts, built with Aragon tools. DNT holders stake the token to vote on which districts are listed and how they are run.
doas: Doğuş Otomotiv is a Turkish car importer and distributor based in Istanbul, founded in 1994. It sells Volkswagen Group brands in Turkey, including Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche and Škoda, through a dealer network and also offers after-sales service.
doc: Healthpeak Properties is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns healthcare buildings: outpatient medical offices, life-science research labs and senior housing. Founded in 1985, it rents them to hospital systems, doctors and biotech companies.
doc-at: DO & CO is an Austrian catering and hospitality company from Vienna, founded in 1981 by Attila Doğudan. It prepares meals for airlines, caters major sports events such as Formula 1, and runs restaurants and hotels.
docn: DigitalOcean is an American cloud provider founded in New York in 2011. It offers developers and smaller companies simple virtual servers (Droplets), managed databases, storage and GPU capacity for running AI applications.
docs: Doximity is a US digital platform for doctors based in San Francisco, often called "LinkedIn for physicians". It offers medical news, telehealth tools, an AI assistant and job search for healthcare professionals.
docu: Docusign is a US software company from San Francisco, founded in 2003. It is best known for electronic signatures, letting people sign contracts online, and also sells software to create, manage and analyze agreements.
dodo: DODO is a decentralized exchange on Ethereum, BNB Chain and other networks that uses its own Proactive Market Maker (PMM) algorithm with oracle prices. It aims to let users trade with less price slippage, and DODO is its governance token.
dog: Dog (Bitcoin), or DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON, is a memecoin native to the Bitcoin blockchain, issued in 2024 under the Runes standard. Tokens were airdropped to holders of a rare-sat artifact with no team sale, and it is pitched as a way to bring new people to Bitcoin.
doge: Dogecoin is the first famous memecoin, created in 2013 by Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer as a joke based on the Shiba Inu dog meme. It is used for payments and tipping, and Elon Musk's posts boosted its fame.
dogeking: DogeKing (DOGEKING) is a Dogecoin-themed meme token with a reflection mechanism: a fee on each transfer is shared out to holders, who receive DOGE simply for holding DOGEKING in their wallets.
doginme: doginme (DOGINME) is a dog-themed memecoin on Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network from Coinbase, built around the 'dog in me' meme. It is a community token with no utility beyond trading.
dogs: DOGS is a memecoin on the TON blockchain inspired by Spotty, a dog drawn by Telegram founder Pavel Durov. In 2024 the token was airdropped to millions of Telegram users based on their activity in the messenger.
dolo: Dolomite is a decentralized money market and margin trading protocol, launched on Arbitrum, where users can lend, borrow and trade a wide range of tokens while keeping the rewards of deposited assets. DOLO is the protocol's token for governance and incentives.
dom: Dom Development is one of Poland's largest homebuilders, founded in 1996 in Warsaw. It builds residential estates in Warsaw, Wrocław, the Tricity and Kraków and sells apartments to private buyers.
domrf: DOM.RF is Russia's state development institution for housing. It refinances mortgages and issues mortgage-backed bonds, runs Bank DOM.RF, and supports housing construction and government mortgage programmes.
dood: DOOD is the token of Doodles, an entertainment brand that grew out of a popular NFT collection of colorful pastel characters launched in 2021. Doodles creates original stories, animation, music, live events and merchandise.
doosan-enerbility: Doosan Enerbility, formerly Doosan Heavy Industries & Construction, is a South Korean power equipment maker based in Changwon and part of the Doosan Group. It builds nuclear reactor components, gas and steam turbines and wind turbines, and is developing small modular reactors.
dos: DAPPOS (DOS) is a protocol that simplifies using blockchains through «intents»: the user only states what they want to do, and the network finds the way to execute it across different blockchains. DOS is the token of this ecosystem.
dot: Polkadot is a multi-chain network that joins separate blockchains into one system with cross-chain messaging and shared security. It was created by Ethereum co-founder Gavin Wood; DOT is used for staking, governance and paying for network resources.
dov: Dover Corporation is a US industrial group from Illinois, founded in 1955. It makes pumps, fuelling-station equipment, refrigerated display cases for supermarkets, fluid-handling components and packaging machinery.
dovu: DOVU is a British project on the Hedera network that brings environmental data and carbon credits on-chain. It helps farmers and companies record and verify sustainability data and trade carbon offsets transparently; DOVU is the network's token.
dow: Dow Inc. is a US chemical giant from Midland, Michigan, founded in 1897 by Herbert Dow. It makes plastics such as polyethylene, silicones, industrial chemicals and coatings used in packaging, construction, cars and household goods.
dpi: DeFi Pulse Index (DPI) is an index token launched in 2020 by Index Coop and DeFi Pulse that holds a basket of leading DeFi governance tokens on Ethereum, such as Uniswap and Aave. One DPI gives exposure to the whole basket, which is rebalanced regularly.
dpz: Domino's is the world's largest pizza chain by sales, founded in Michigan in 1960 by brothers Tom and James Monaghan. It works mostly through franchisees in more than 90 countries and is known for delivery and online ordering.
dr-sulaiman-al-habib: Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Group is the largest private hospital operator in Saudi Arabia, based in Riyadh and founded by physician Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib. It runs hospitals, clinics, pharmacies and home care in the Kingdom, and also has hospitals in the UAE and Bahrain.
drb: DebtReliefBot (DRB) is a memecoin on Base that was created in March 2025 when xAI's chatbot Grok was asked on X to launch a token through the Bankr bot. Trading fees from the token go to a wallet linked to Grok.
dreams: Daydreams (DREAMS) is the token of Daydreams, an open-source framework for building AI agents that act on blockchains, for example trading or playing on-chain games. It works with many networks and agent tools and is released under the MIT licence.
drg: DragonSwap is a decentralized exchange on the Sei blockchain where users swap tokens and provide liquidity. DRG is its token, used for governance and to reward liquidity providers.
dri: Darden Restaurants is the largest operator of full-service restaurants in the US, based in Orlando, Florida. It owns the Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, The Capital Grille, Yard House and Ruth's Chris Steak House chains.
drift: Drift Protocol is one of the largest decentralized exchanges on Solana, offering perpetual futures, spot trading, lending and borrowing in one app. DRIFT is its governance token, used to vote on how the protocol is run.
drreddy: Dr. Reddy's Laboratories is an Indian pharmaceutical company from Hyderabad, founded by Anji Reddy in 1984. It makes generic medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients and biosimilars, selling them in India, the US, Russia and Europe.
drv: Derive (formerly Lyra) is a decentralized protocol for options, perpetual futures and structured products, running on its own Derive Chain built on the OP Stack. DRV is the governance token: holders steer the protocol and receive a share of fee revenue.
dsct: Israel Discount Bank is one of Israel's largest banks, based in Tel Aviv and founded in 1935 by Leon Recanati. It serves households and businesses, owns Mercantile Bank and the Cal credit card company, and operates in the US through IDB Bank in New York.
dsv: DSV is a Danish transport and logistics company based in Hedehusene, founded in 1976 by independent truck owners. It is one of the world's largest freight forwarders, arranging air, sea and road shipments and running warehouses, and grew further by buying DB Schenker in 2025.
dsy: Dassault Systèmes is a French 3D design software company founded in 1981 as part of the Dassault group. Engineers in aerospace, automotive and machinery use its CATIA and SOLIDWORKS programs; it also makes software for life sciences and simulation.
dsync: Destra Network (DSYNC) is a decentralized network for AI: it offers infrastructure to run autonomous agents, decentralized computing and privacy tools in one ecosystem. DSYNC is its deflationary utility token used to pay for services.
dt: Dynatrace is a software company founded in 2005 in Linz, Austria, now headquartered in Massachusetts. Its AI-driven platform monitors applications and cloud infrastructure, helping companies spot and fix outages and slowdowns.
dte: DTE Energy is an energy company from Detroit that supplies electricity and natural gas to millions of customers in Michigan. It also develops wind and solar farms and runs energy projects for industry.
dte-de: Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecom company, based in Bonn, and the former state postal and telephone network of Germany. It provides mobile and internet services in Germany and across Europe and controls the US operator T-Mobile US.
dtec: Dtec (DTEC) is a token on Polygon linked to Dtec, a software component installed in the operating system of vehicles and smart platforms to communicate with the vehicle and control its equipment and remote IoT devices.
dtg: Daimler Truck, based in Stuttgart, is the world's largest maker of trucks and buses; it was spun off from Daimler in 2021. Its brands include Mercedes-Benz Trucks, Freightliner, Western Star, Fuso and Setra buses.
dtm: DT Midstream is a US company from Detroit that owns natural gas pipelines, storage facilities and gathering systems. It was spun off from utility DTE Energy in 2021, and its main assets are in the Appalachian Basin and Louisiana.
dual: Dual is a tokenization engine for real-world assets that lets businesses build programmable tokens for anything from currencies and loyalty points to real estate, treasuries and physical products. DUAL is the utility token that powers the ecosystem.
duk: Duke Energy is one of the largest US utilities, based in Charlotte, North Carolina. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of customers in the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest, sells natural gas, and runs a large nuclear fleet.
duol: Duolingo is a language-learning platform from Pittsburgh founded in 2011 by Luis von Ahn and Severin Hacker. Its app with the green owl Duo teaches dozens of languages through short game-like lessons, plus maths, music and chess.
dusk: Dusk (DUSK) is a layer-1 blockchain from the Netherlands built for regulated financial markets. It lets tokenized securities be issued and traded in line with EU law while protecting privacy; DUSK is used for fees and staking.
dva: DaVita is a US company from Denver and one of the largest operators of dialysis clinics in the US for people with chronic kidney failure. Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway is among its investors.
dvec: Far Eastern Energy Company (DEK) is a power and heat retailer in Russia's Far East, part of the RusHydro group. It sells electricity and heat to households and businesses in Primorye, Khabarovsk Krai, Amur Region and other areas.
dvn: Devon Energy is a US oil and gas producer from Oklahoma City, founded in 1971. It extracts oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids from US shale fields, above all the Delaware Basin of the Permian.
dvo: Divo (DVO) is the token of DIVO, a SocialFi network for the fashion and advertising industry. Creators, agencies and brands use it to publish work, protect ownership of their content with AI tools, get paid and collaborate across borders without intermediaries.
dxcm: DexCom is an American medical technology company from San Diego that makes continuous glucose monitoring systems for people with diabetes. A small sensor on the skin sends sugar levels to a phone or watch every few minutes, without finger pricks.
dy: Dycom Industries is a Florida contractor that builds and maintains telecommunications infrastructure. It lays fibre-optic cable, installs wireless and cable networks for major US carriers and provides engineering and maintenance services.
dydx: dYdX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, founded in 2017 by former Coinbase engineer Antonio Juliano. It now runs on its own blockchain in the Cosmos ecosystem; the DYDX token is used for staking, network security and governance.
dym: Dymension is a modular layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK that makes it easy to launch custom rollups called RollApps. It gives them shared security, liquidity and interoperability, and DYM is used for staking, fees and governance.
east: Eastern Company is Egypt's largest cigarette maker, founded in 1920 and based in Giza, with the state as main shareholder. It produces local brands such as Cleopatra, shisha tobacco and cigars, and manufactures cigarettes for international tobacco companies.
eat: Brinker International is an American restaurant company based in Dallas. It owns the casual-dining chains Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy, which operate in the US and other countries.
eat-pl: AmRest is a restaurant operator founded in Wrocław, Poland, in 1993 and now headquartered in Madrid. It runs thousands of restaurants across Europe as a franchisee of KFC, Pizza Hut, Burger King and Starbucks, and also owns brands such as La Tagliatella and Sushi Shop.
ebay: eBay is a US online marketplace from San Jose, California, founded in 1995 by Pierre Omidyar. Millions of sellers and buyers trade new and used goods on it, from collectible cards to car parts, by auction or at a fixed price.
ebo: EBOS Group is a healthcare and animal care distributor founded in New Zealand in 1922 and listed in both New Zealand and Australia. It is one of the region's largest wholesalers of medicines to pharmacies and hospitals and also owns pet food and animal care brands such as Black Hawk.
ebro: Ebro Foods is a Spanish food company based in Madrid and one of the world's largest rice and pasta groups. Its brands include Brillante, SOS and Tilda rice, Minute Rice and Garofalo pasta.
ebs: Erste Group is an Austrian banking group based in Vienna whose roots go back to the country's first savings bank, founded in 1819. It is one of the largest banks in Central and Eastern Europe, with banks such as Česká spořitelna, Slovenská sporiteľňa and BCR.
echo: EchoStar is a US telecom company from Colorado that merged with DISH Network. It runs DISH satellite TV, the Sling TV streaming service, HughesNet satellite internet and the Boost Mobile wireless brand.
ecl: Ecolab is a US company based in Saint Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1923, that provides water treatment, cleaning, hygiene and infection-prevention products and services. Its customers include restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food plants and factories; it also owns Nalco Water.
ecmpa: Eurocommercial Properties is a Dutch real-estate investment company based in Amsterdam. It owns and manages large shopping centres anchored by supermarkets and hypermarkets in Italy, France, Sweden and Belgium, earning income from shop rents.
ecte: EurocoinToken (ECTE) is a token created for micropayments and international transactions through the Eurocoinpay payment gateway, aimed mainly at brick-and-mortar shops and their customers who want to pay for goods and services in crypto.
ed: Consolidated Edison (Con Edison) is a New York utility with a history dating back to 1823. It supplies electricity, gas and steam to millions of customers in New York City and Westchester County; its Manhattan steam system is one of the largest in the world.
edel: Edel Finance is an on-chain lending network for tokenized stocks. Holders of tokenized shares from issuers such as Ondo and xStocks can lend them out for yield, while traders borrow them to build long or short positions without perpetual futures.
eden: OpenEden is a Singapore-based real-world asset tokenization platform that issues TBILL, a token backed by short-term US Treasury bills. It has also launched the USDO stablecoin; EDEN is the ecosystem token.
edena: EDENA is the token of EDENA Capital Partners, which runs a platform for security token offerings (STOs). It tokenizes real estate, carbon credits, government bonds, ETFs and REITs so investors can buy small fractions and trade them around the clock.
edn: Edenor (Empresa Distribuidora y Comercializadora Norte) is Argentina's largest electricity distributor, based in Buenos Aires. Created in 1992 in the privatisation of the state power company, it supplies electricity to millions of customers in the northern part of Buenos Aires city and its northern and western suburbs.
edp: EDP (Energias de Portugal) is Portugal's largest electricity company, based in Lisbon. It generates power, runs distribution grids in Portugal, Spain and Brazil, sells energy to homes and businesses, and through EDP Renováveis builds wind and solar farms worldwide.
edpr: EDP Renováveis is a Madrid-based renewable energy company, part of Portugal's EDP group. It develops, builds and operates wind farms and solar plants across Europe, North America, South America and Asia and sells the electricity they produce.
edu: Open Campus (EDU) is a protocol building blockchain infrastructure for education: digital diplomas and certificates and funding for educational content. The project is backed by Animoca Brands and runs its own network, EDU Chain.
eeft: Euronet Worldwide is a US payments company based in Kansas, founded in 1994 in Budapest. It runs ATM networks, sells prepaid mobile top-ups and digital content, and owns the Ria money transfer service.
eem: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets (EEM) is a BlackRock ETF holding large companies from emerging markets, including China, India and Taiwan.
efa: iShares MSCI EAFE (EFA) invests in large companies from Europe, Australasia and the Far East, excluding the US and Canada.
efi: ElevateFi (EFI) is a DeFi protocol on Polygon offering non-custodial staking vaults, validator delegation and liquidity strategies, including optional pools of real-world assets. A DAO of token holders votes on proposals.
efih: e-finance for Digital and Financial Investments is an Egyptian fintech group based in Cairo, founded in 2005. It built and runs much of the government's digital payment infrastructure, such as salary, tax and customs payments, and owns consumer payment services like khales.
efx: Equifax is one of the three major US credit bureaus, founded in 1899 in Atlanta. It collects credit histories of millions of people and businesses, sells credit reports and scores to lenders and verifies income and employment; in 2017 it suffered a huge data breach.
eg: Everest Group is a reinsurance and insurance company based in Bermuda, founded in 1973. It takes on risks from other insurers worldwide and sells property, casualty and specialty insurance to businesses.
egie3: Engie Brasil Energia is one of Brazil's largest private power generators, based in Florianópolis and controlled by France's Engie. It runs hydroelectric, wind and solar plants, trades electricity with large consumers and is expanding into power transmission and gas pipelines.
egl: Mota-Engil is a Portuguese construction and engineering group based in Porto. It builds roads, railways, ports, dams and buildings in Europe, Africa and Latin America and is also active in mining services, waste and energy.
egl1: EGL1 is a meme token built around a bald eagle and American patriotic imagery that calls itself the first superhero meme. It has no practical use beyond its community and trades as a memecoin.
egld: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a layer-1 blockchain from Romania that uses sharding for high throughput. Launched in 2020, it supports smart contracts and DeFi; EGLD pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
egp: EastGroup Properties is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Jackson, Mississippi. It develops, owns and leases warehouse and light-industrial buildings in fast-growing Sunbelt cities, especially in Texas, Florida, California and Arizona.
ehc: Encompass Health is a US chain of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals based in Birmingham, Alabama. Its hospitals help patients recover after strokes, injuries, surgery and serious illness; the company was formerly called HealthSouth.
eichermot: Eicher Motors is an Indian automotive company from New Delhi best known as the owner of Royal Enfield, the motorcycle brand famous for the Bullet and Classic models. Through VE Commercial Vehicles, a joint venture with Sweden's Volvo Group, it also makes trucks and buses.
eigen: EigenCloud (formerly EigenLayer) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum: staked ETH is reused to secure other services and networks. The project was founded by Sreeram Kannan, and the EIGEN token is used for governance and to back guarantees for its verifiable cloud services.
eix: Edison International is a California power company whose main subsidiary, Southern California Edison, supplies electricity to millions of people in Southern California. It is developing the grid, energy storage and infrastructure for electric vehicles.
ekgyo: Emlak Konut is a Turkish real estate developer from Istanbul linked to the state housing agency TOKİ. It develops large residential and commercial projects on state land, mostly in Istanbul, working with private builders on a revenue-sharing model.
ekubo: Ekubo Protocol (EKUBO) is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity that started on Starknet and also runs on Ethereum. It keeps all pools in a single contract to cut gas costs and lets developers add custom «extensions» to pools; EKUBO is its governance token.
el: The Estée Lauder Companies is an American beauty group based in New York, founded in 1946 by Estée Lauder and her husband Joseph. It makes skin care, makeup, fragrance and hair-care products under brands such as Estée Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, Bobbi Brown, Jo Malone London and Tom Ford Beauty.
el-fr: EssilorLuxottica is a French-Italian eyewear giant formed in 2018 by the merger of Essilor and Luxottica. It makes spectacle lenses, frames and sunglasses under brands like Ray-Ban and Oakley, runs optical chains such as Sunglass Hut and makes smart glasses with Meta.
el-token: ELYSIA is a peer-to-peer real-estate investment platform that tokenises properties so many people can co-invest in a building with small amounts and connects sellers with buyers. EL is the platform's token used within its ecosystem.
ela: Elastos is a blockchain platform founded by operating-system veteran Rong Chen to build a user-owned "SmartWeb". Its main chain is merge-mined with Bitcoin, borrowing Bitcoin's hash power for security, and ELA pays for transactions and services in the ecosystem.
elan: Elanco is a US animal health company from Indianapolis that makes medicines and vaccines for pets and farm animals. It was spun off from Eli Lilly and is known for products such as the Seresto flea and tick collar.
ele: Endesa is Spain's largest electricity company, headquartered in Madrid and controlled by Italy's Enel. It generates power at nuclear, gas, hydro and solar plants, owns distribution grids and supplies electricity and gas to millions of customers.
elephant: Elephant Money is a DeFi protocol on BNB Chain built around the ELEPHANT token and its TRUNK stablecoin. Its treasury and token mechanics are meant to fund yield for users holding and staking these tokens.
elf: aelf (ELF) is a layer-1 blockchain from Singapore, launched in 2017, built with a main chain and side chains for scaling. Smart contracts are written in C#, and the project focuses on AI tools for developers.
elf-etf: e.l.f. Beauty is an affordable cosmetics company from Oakland, California, founded in 2004. It owns the brands e.l.f. Cosmetics, e.l.f. SKIN, Naturium, Well People and Rhode, selling make-up and skincare online and in mass retailers.
elfv: EL5-Energo (formerly Enel Russia) is a Russian power generator. It runs large thermal power plants such as Konakovo GRES, Nevinnomyssk GRES and Sredneuralsk GRES and has wind power projects; Italy's Enel sold it in 2023.
elg: Escoin (ELG) is a crypto project aimed at the legal sector: it wants to give law firms and their clients a shared digital infrastructure to work together across borders, with the token used inside that network.
eli: Elia Group is a Belgian electricity grid company based in Brussels. It runs Belgium's high-voltage transmission network through Elia and, through 50Hertz, part of Germany's grid, connecting large amounts of offshore wind power.
elisa: Elisa is a Finnish telecom company based in Helsinki. It provides mobile, broadband and TV services to consumers and businesses in Finland and Estonia, and sells software and digital services to telecom operators abroad.
elizaos: ElizaOS is an open-source framework for building autonomous AI agents that can talk on social networks and act on blockchains. The project grew out of ai16z, and the ELIZAOS token is used for governance and ecosystem growth.
elm: Elm is a Saudi technology company from Riyadh owned by the Public Investment Fund (PIF). It builds digital government services, including the Absher platform for passports, visas and driving licences, as well as IT and security solutions for businesses.
elmt: Element is Russia's largest microelectronics group, created in 2019 by Sistema and Rostec. It designs and makes microchips, semiconductor components and electronic modules; its plants include Mikron in Zelenograd.
elp: Elympics (ELP) is a gaming platform for skill-based competitive games, where players join tournaments and win prizes based on how well they play. ELP is its utility and governance token, used for game and tournament entry, staking by the nodes that verify matches, and voting.
elpe: HELLENiQ ENERGY, formerly Hellenic Petroleum, is a Greek energy company from Athens. It runs oil refineries in Aspropyrgos, Elefsina and Thessaloniki, sells fuel through EKO and BP-branded stations in Greece and is building solar and wind power.
els: Equity LifeStyle Properties is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from Chicago, founded by Sam Zell. It owns manufactured-home communities, RV resorts and marinas, mostly in Florida, California and Arizona, and earns rent from residents and campers.
elsa: HeyElsa is an AI platform that turns plain-language requests into on-chain actions: swaps, bridges, staking, yield search and portfolio management across many networks. It offers an AI copilot for users and widgets, an SDK and APIs for businesses.
elux-b: Electrolux is a Swedish household appliance maker headquartered in Stockholm, founded in 1919. It makes refrigerators, washing machines, dishwashers and cookers sold worldwide under brands such as Electrolux, AEG and Frigidaire.
elv: Elevance Health (Anthem until 2022) is one of the largest US health insurers, based in Indianapolis. It sells health plans under the Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield brand, serves Medicare and Medicaid programs and runs the CarelonRx pharmacy business.
embj3: Embraer is a Brazilian aerospace company founded in 1969 and based in São José dos Campos. It is one of the world's leading makers of regional jets such as the E-Jets E2, builds Phenom and Praetor business jets and the C-390 military transport, and its subsidiary Eve is developing electric air taxis.
emblem: Emblem Vault is a platform that wraps crypto assets from many blockchains, including Bitcoin Ordinals and Counterparty tokens, into tradable NFT vaults. This lets assets from one chain be bought and sold on marketplaces of another; the Emblem token belongs to its ecosystem.
eme: EMCOR Group is a US construction company from Connecticut that installs electrical, mechanical and plumbing systems in buildings. It works on data centres, factories, hospitals and offices and also maintains the systems of existing buildings.
emfd: Emaar Misr is an Egyptian real estate developer based in Cairo and a subsidiary of Dubai's Emaar Properties. It builds large residential and resort communities such as Uptown Cairo, Mivida and Marassi on the North Coast.
emr: Emerson Electric is a US industrial technology company based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 1890. It makes automation systems, control valves, measurement instruments and industrial software used by factories, refineries, chemical and power plants.
en: Bouygues is a French industrial group based in Paris, founded in 1952 by Francis Bouygues. It works in construction (Bouygues Construction and road builder Colas), energy and services (Equans), telecoms through Bouygues Telecom, and media through the TV channel TF1.
ena: Ethena is an Ethereum protocol that issues USDe, a synthetic dollar kept stable by crypto collateral and hedging with futures. ENA is the protocol's governance token; the project was founded by Guy Young.
ena-pl: Enea is a state-controlled Polish energy group based in Poznań. It generates power, notably at the large Kozienice power plant, owns the Bogdanka coal mine and supplies electricity to millions of customers in western Poland.
enb: Enbridge is a Canadian energy company from Calgary that runs one of North America's largest networks of oil and gas pipelines. It also supplies natural gas to homes in Ontario and develops wind and solar power.
enel: Enel is Italy's largest energy company, based in Rome and founded in 1962 as the state power monopoly. It generates electricity, including renewables through Enel Green Power, owns power grids and sells electricity and gas in Italy, Spain (Endesa) and Latin America.
enelam: Enel Américas is a Santiago-based electricity company controlled by Italy's Enel. It generates power from hydro, wind, solar and thermal plants and distributes electricity to millions of customers, mainly in Brazil and Colombia, as well as in Central America.
enelchile: Enel Chile is one of Chile's largest electricity companies, based in Santiago and controlled by Italy's Enel. It generates power from hydro, wind, solar, geothermal and gas plants and, through Enel Distribución, supplies electricity to most of the Santiago metropolitan area.
enev3: Eneva is a Brazilian energy company based in Rio de Janeiro. It produces natural gas onshore in the Parnaíba Basin in Maranhão and in Amazonas and burns it in its own nearby thermal power plants (a 'reservoir-to-wire' model), and also runs LNG, solar and gas-supply businesses.
eng: Enagás is a Spanish energy infrastructure company from Madrid and the technical operator of Spain's gas system. It owns and runs gas pipelines, LNG regasification terminals and underground storage, and is developing hydrogen networks.
engi: Engie is a French energy company based in Paris, formed from Gaz de France and Suez. It generates electricity, much of it from renewables, owns gas networks and storage in France and provides energy services to cities and businesses.
engi11: Energisa is a Brazilian electricity group with roots in Cataguases, Minas Gerais, dating back to 1905. It runs power distribution companies serving millions of customers in states such as Mato Grosso, Tocantins, Paraíba and Sergipe, and also builds transmission lines and sells solar distributed generation; ENGI11 is a unit of its shares.
eni: Eni is an Italian energy company based in Rome, founded in 1953 by Enrico Mattei. It produces oil and gas in dozens of countries, especially in Africa, refines fuel, sells gas and electricity through Plenitude and is growing renewable energy and biofuels.
enj: Enjin Coin (ENJ) is the token of the Enjin ecosystem, which has been building infrastructure for in-game NFT items since 2017. Developers issue in-game objects on Enjin's own blockchain, and ENJ is used to create them, pay fees and stake.
enjsa: Enerjisa Enerji is Turkey's largest electricity distribution and retail company, based in Istanbul and jointly owned by Sabancı Holding and Germany's E.ON. It runs power grids and supplies electricity in regions including Istanbul's Asian side, Ankara and Adana.
enkai: Enka İnşaat is a Turkish construction and engineering company based in Istanbul, founded in 1957. It builds power plants, infrastructure and commercial buildings in Turkey, Russia, Europe and Asia, and also owns gas-fired power plants and office and retail property it leases out.
enlt: Enlight Renewable Energy is an Israeli clean energy company based in Rosh HaAyin. It develops, builds and operates wind farms, solar parks and battery storage projects in Israel, Europe and the United States, where it works through its subsidiary Clenera.
enpg: En+ Group is a Russian energy and metals company founded by Oleg Deripaska. It owns large hydroelectric plants on the Angara and Yenisei rivers in Siberia and a controlling stake in aluminium producer Rusal.
enph: Enphase Energy is a US solar technology company from Fremont, California, founded in 2006. It pioneered microinverters that convert power at each solar panel, and sells home batteries, EV chargers and software for rooftop solar systems worldwide.
enr: Siemens Energy is a German energy equipment maker based in Munich, spun off from Siemens in 2020. It builds gas turbines, power grid equipment and transformers, and wind turbines through Siemens Gamesa.
ens: Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is a domain name system on Ethereum that replaces long wallet addresses with readable names like name.eth. The service launched in 2017 under Nick Johnson; ENS is the governance token of its DAO.
ens-etf: EnerSys is a Pennsylvania-based maker of industrial batteries and energy storage systems. Its batteries power telecom networks, data centers, forklifts and warehouse vehicles, as well as military and aerospace equipment.
ensg: Ensign Group is a US company from California that runs skilled nursing homes, senior living communities and rehabilitation centers. Its separate Standard Bearer unit owns the real estate of many of these facilities.
enso: Enso is a network that brings different blockchains together in one access point for developers: its API and tools let them read data and build and execute transactions with DeFi protocols across many chains. ENSO is the network token.
ent: Entain is a British sports-betting and gaming company based in London. It owns brands such as Ladbrokes, Coral, bwin and partypoker, runs betting shops and online platforms in many countries, and owns half of BetMGM in the United States.
entel: Entel (Empresa Nacional de Telecomunicaciones) is a Chilean telecommunications company based in Santiago and one of the country's largest mobile operators. It provides mobile, fibre internet and IT services to consumers and businesses in Chile and also runs a mobile network in Peru.
entg: Entegris is a US supplier of specialty materials for chipmaking based in Massachusetts. It provides semiconductor fabs with ultra-pure chemicals, filters, wafer carriers and contamination-control solutions.
eoan: E.ON is one of Europe's largest energy companies, based in Essen, Germany. It runs electricity and gas distribution grids in Germany and other countries and supplies energy to tens of millions of customers.
eog: EOG Resources is a US oil and gas producer based in Houston, formerly Enron Oil & Gas, which split from Enron in 1999. It extracts oil and natural gas mainly from shale fields in Texas and other US states.
epam: EPAM Systems is a US software engineering and IT consulting company from Newtown, Pennsylvania, founded in 1993 by Arkadiy Dobkin and Leo Lozner. Its tens of thousands of engineers build and modernise software, cloud and AI systems for large companies worldwide.
epi-a: Epiroc is a Swedish maker of equipment for mining and infrastructure, based in Stockholm and spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018. It produces drill rigs, rock excavation and loading machines, tools and automation, plus service and spare parts for mines worldwide.
epic: Epic Cash (EPIC) is private digital cash built on the MimbleWimble protocol, which hides transaction amounts and participants. The coin is created by mining and had no pre-allocation to its founders.
epol: iShares MSCI Poland (EPOL) invests in Poland's largest listed companies: banks, energy firms and retailers.
epr: EPR Properties is a Kansas City-based REIT that specializes in leisure and entertainment real estate. It owns movie theaters, entertainment centers, ski resorts, water parks and other attractions, leased to operators on long-term contracts.
ept: Balance (EPT) is the native token of Balance, an AI and Web3 protocol for social and gaming experiences built around AI companions and "Key Nodes". EPT is used for governance, staking and payments; backers include a16z, Galaxy Interactive and Animoca Brands.
eqh: Equitable Holdings is a US financial services company from New York, whose Equitable insurer dates back to 1859. It sells annuities, life insurance and retirement plans and owns a majority of the asset manager AllianceBernstein.
eqix: Equinix is the world's largest colocation data center operator, based in Redwood City, California, and founded in 1998. It rents server space in dozens of major cities and links the networks of cloud providers, banks and telecoms; it is structured as a REIT.
eqnr: Equinor, formerly Statoil, is Norway's state-controlled energy company based in Stavanger. It is the largest operator on the Norwegian continental shelf, running fields such as Johan Sverdrup, is one of Europe's main natural gas suppliers and also builds offshore wind farms; this is its Oslo-listed share.
eqt: EQT Corporation is the largest natural gas producer in the United States, headquartered in Pittsburgh. It extracts gas from the Appalachian Basin shale (Marcellus and Utica) and owns pipelines to transport it.
eqt-se: EQT is a Swedish investment firm based in Stockholm, founded in 1994 with backing from the Wallenberg family's Investor AB. It manages private equity, infrastructure and real estate funds, buying and developing companies on behalf of pension funds and other investors.
eqtl3: Equatorial is a Brazilian energy group from Brasília. It runs electricity distribution networks in several Brazilian states, owns transmission lines and renewable plants, and has expanded into sanitation and telecoms.
era: Caldera is a rollup-as-a-service platform that helps projects launch their own layer-2 chains on Ethereum, plus Metalayer to connect them. ERA is the token for staking, payments and governance.
eregl: Erdemir (Ereğli Demir Çelik) is Turkey's largest steelmaker, founded in 1960 in Ereğli on the Black Sea coast. Together with its subsidiary İsdemir it produces flat steel for cars, shipbuilding, home appliances and pipes; its controlling shareholder is the OYAK group.
erf: Eurofins Scientific is a laboratory testing group headquartered in Luxembourg, founded in 1987 in Nantes, France. Through a global network of labs it tests food, water, the environment, medicines and clinical samples for safety, quality and authenticity.
erg: Ergo is a proof-of-work blockchain launched in 2019 with the eUTXO model and powerful smart contracts for DeFi and financial tools. ERG is mined, and the network is known for its focus on decentralization with no pre-mine.
eric-b: Ericsson is a Swedish telecom equipment maker based in Stockholm, founded in 1876 by Lars Magnus Ericsson. It supplies mobile network gear such as 5G radio equipment, software and services to telecom operators around the world.
erie: Erie Indemnity is a US company from Erie, Pennsylvania, founded in 1925. It manages the Erie Insurance Exchange, handling sales, underwriting and policy services for its home, auto, business and life insurance in exchange for a management fee.
ern: Ethos Reserve Note (ERN) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin from Ethos Reserve, a DeFi protocol on Optimism. Users mint ERN by locking crypto such as ETH as collateral worth more than the loan, which is how it aims to stay near $1.
es: Eversource Energy is New England's largest energy company, headquartered in Boston and Hartford. It delivers electricity, natural gas and water to millions of customers in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire.
esab: ESAB makes equipment and consumables for welding and cutting metal. It was founded in Sweden in 1904 by inventor Oscar Kjellberg; today it is headquartered in the US and became independent from Colfax in 2022.
ese: Eesee is a Web3 marketplace where people can win NFTs, tokens and other assets through prize draws and drops instead of paying full price. ESE is the platform token, used for rewards and perks.
eslt: Elbit Systems is Israel's largest defence company, based in Haifa. It develops drones such as the Hermes family, avionics and pilot helmets, electronic warfare and communications systems, artillery and munitions for the Israeli military and export customers.
esnt: Essent Group is a Bermuda-registered insurer that provides private mortgage insurance in the United States. It protects lenders against losses when borrowers with small down payments default, and also offers reinsurance and title insurance.
esp: Espresso (ESP) is a transaction-confirmation network for layer-2 blockchains based on BFT consensus. It gives rollups a near-instant, reliable view of each other's state, making interaction between chains easier and protecting against block reorgs.
esports: Yooldo Games (ESPORTS) is a Web3 gaming platform that works across Ethereum, Linea and BNB Chain and aims to make blockchain games easy to start, with play-to-earn games and online tournaments. The ESPORTS token is used for governance, in-game purchases and player rewards.
ess: Essex Property Trust is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in San Mateo, California, founded in 1971. It owns, develops and rents out apartment communities on the West Coast — in Southern and Northern California and the Seattle area.
essity-b: Essity is a Swedish hygiene and health company based in Stockholm, spun off from SCA in 2017. It makes incontinence products, tissue, feminine care and baby care, and medical products, with brands such as TENA, Tork, Libresse, Libero and Leukoplast.
estc: Elastic is the company behind Elasticsearch, a popular open-source search and analytics engine, founded in Amsterdam in 2012. Businesses use its Elastic platform, with tools like Kibana, to search their data, monitor apps and IT systems, and detect security threats.
etc: Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain that kept running after the 2016 hard fork, when most of the community reversed the effects of The DAO hack. ETC sticks to the "code is law" principle and, unlike Ethereum, still uses Proof of Work mining.
ete: National Bank of Greece, founded in 1841 and based in Athens, is one of Greece's largest banks. It provides retail and corporate banking, mortgages, cards and asset management through a nationwide branch network.
etel: Telecom Egypt is Egypt's state-controlled telecom operator based in Cairo. It runs the country's fixed-line and internet network, offers mobile service under the WE brand, operates international subsea cables and owns a large stake in Vodafone Egypt.
eternal: Eternal (formerly Zomato) is an Indian internet company based in Gurugram, founded in 2008. It runs the Zomato food delivery app, the Blinkit quick-commerce grocery service, District for bookings and tickets, and Hyperpure, which supplies restaurants.
eth: Ether (ETH) is the coin of Ethereum, the biggest smart-contract platform, which hosts DeFi, NFTs and stablecoins. Ether pays the network's transaction fees; Ethereum was co-founded by Vitalik Buterin in 2015.
etha: iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) is BlackRock's spot ether ETF, launched in 2024, giving brokerage-account access to ETH, the coin of the Ethereum network.
ethdydx: This is the original Ethereum version (ERC-20) of the DYDX token, issued in 2021 for the dYdX derivatives exchange. dYdX later moved to its own blockchain, where DYDX is the native token, and the Ethereum version can be bridged to it.
ethfi: Ether.fi is a liquid restaking protocol on Ethereum that is also growing into a crypto neobank with a card for spending and saving. Users stake ETH and keep it liquid through the eETH token; ETHFI is the governance token.
ethw: EthereumPoW (ETHW) is a fork of Ethereum created in September 2022, when the main network switched from mining to proof of stake. Some miners kept running the old proof-of-work chain, and ETHW is its native coin.
etln: Etalon Group is a Russian residential property developer founded in 1987 in St Petersburg, now controlled by AFK Sistema. It builds apartment complexes in Moscow, St Petersburg and other Russian cities.
etn: Eaton is a power management company legally domiciled in Dublin, with roots going back to 1911 in the United States. It makes electrical equipment for buildings, data centers and utility grids, as well as components for aircraft and vehicles.
etn-token: Electroneum is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain with transactions in a few seconds and instant finality. Founded in the UK by Richard Ells, the project targets mobile users and payments in developing countries; ETN is its native coin.
etor: eToro is an online trading and investing platform from Israel, founded in 2007 by brothers Yoni and Ronen Assia with David Ring. Known for social trading and its CopyTrader feature, it lets users buy stocks, ETFs and crypto and follow or copy other investors.
etr: Entergy is a US utility from New Orleans, Louisiana. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas and operates several nuclear power plants.
etsy: Etsy is a US online marketplace from Brooklyn, New York, founded in 2005. Millions of independent sellers use it to sell handmade, vintage and creative goods such as jewellery, home decor, art and craft supplies; the company also owns the resale app Depop.
eul: Euler is a DeFi lending protocol on Ethereum where users supply and borrow crypto assets. Its second version lets anyone create their own lending markets with custom risk settings; EUL is the governance token.
eurc: EURC is a euro-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, the company behind USDC. Each token is backed one-to-one by euro reserves, it is issued under the EU's MiCA rules, and it runs on Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Base and other blockchains.
eurcv: EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) is a euro stablecoin issued by SG-FORGE, the digital-assets subsidiary of French bank Société Générale. Each token aims to equal one euro and is backed by reserves; it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum.
eure: EURe is a euro stablecoin issued by Monerium, a licensed electronic money institution from Iceland. Each token is regulated e-money backed one-to-one by euros and can move on Ethereum, Gnosis, Polygon and other networks or be redeemed via a bank IBAN.
eurob: Eurobank is one of Greece's four largest banks, based in Athens. It offers retail and corporate banking, mortgages, cards and wealth management in Greece and also operates in Cyprus, Bulgaria and Luxembourg.
europ: EURØP is a euro stablecoin compliant with the EU's MiCA rules, issued by a licensed French issuer supervised by the regulator ACPR. Each token is backed 1:1 by euros held at EU banks such as Société Générale and can be redeemed for euros.
eurq: Quantoz EURQ is a euro stablecoin issued by Quantoz Payments, a licensed electronic-money institution in the Netherlands. Each EURQ is meant to equal one euro, is backed by reserves and is issued under the EU's MiCA rules.
eurs: STASIS EURO (EURS) is a euro stablecoin issued by STASIS, a company based in Malta. Each token is meant to be backed one-to-one by euro reserves, with regular audits, and it is used to hold and move euros on blockchains such as Ethereum.
ev: Everything (EV) is a project that combines several DeFi protocols into one interconnected ecosystem. The EV token is used for governance, for using the services and for capturing value across all of the project's products.
evaa: EVAA Protocol is a decentralized lending protocol on the TON network. Users can supply crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, including directly from Telegram; EVAA is the protocol's governance token.
evd: CTS Eventim is a German live-entertainment company based in Bremen. It runs Eventim, one of Europe's largest ticketing platforms, promotes concerts, tours and festivals, and operates venues and arenas.
evk: Evonik is a German specialty chemicals company based in Essen, created in 2007. It makes additives, high-performance materials and ingredients used in plastics, coatings, animal feed, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.
evn: EVN is an Austrian energy and environmental services company based in Maria Enzersdorf, Lower Austria. It generates and distributes electricity, gas and heat, supplies drinking water, and also runs power grids in Bulgaria and North Macedonia.
evo: Evolution is a Swedish developer of online casino games, founded in 2006 and listed in Stockholm. It streams live dealer games such as roulette, blackjack and game shows like Crazy Time from its studios to online casino operators, and also owns slot studios like NetEnt and Red Tiger.
evr: Evercore is an independent investment bank from New York, founded in 1995 by Roger Altman. It advises companies on mergers and acquisitions, restructurings and raising capital, and also manages wealth.
evrg: Evergy is an electric utility based in Kansas City, Missouri, formed in 2018 by the merger of Westar Energy and Great Plains Energy. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of people in Kansas and Missouri, with a large share coming from wind power.
evrz: Evraz is a steel and mining company with its main plants in Siberia and the Urals in Russia. It is one of the country's biggest steelmakers and a leading producer of railway rails and construction steel, and also mines iron ore and coking coal.
ew: Edwards Lifesciences is a US medical device maker based in Irvine, California. It specialises in artificial heart valves, including the Sapien transcatheter valves that are implanted without open-heart surgery.
ewbc: East West Bancorp is a bank holding company from Pasadena, California, and the owner of East West Bank. The bank serves people and businesses in the US and specializes in financial links between America and Greater China.
ewg: iShares MSCI Germany (EWG) invests in large German companies such as SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom.
ewt: Energy Web Token (EWT) is the native token of Energy Web Chain, an open blockchain for the energy sector from the non-profit Energy Web. Energy companies use it to track renewable power and certificates and to manage distributed devices.
exc: Exelon is one of the largest US utilities, based in Chicago. Through its grid companies ComEd, PECO and BGE, among others, it delivers electricity and gas to millions of customers in Illinois, Pennsylvania, Maryland and Washington, D.C.
exe: Expand Energy is the largest natural gas producer in the United States, formed in 2024 when Chesapeake Energy merged with Southwestern Energy. Based near Houston in Spring, Texas, it produces gas in the Appalachian Marcellus and Utica shales and the Haynesville basin in Louisiana.
exel: Exelixis is a US cancer-drug company from Alameda, California, founded in 1994. Its best-known medicine is cabozantinib, sold as Cabometyx and Cometriq for kidney, liver and thyroid cancers, and it develops new oncology treatments.
exls: EXL Service is a New York company that provides data analytics, artificial intelligence and operations outsourcing. Its main clients are insurers, banks, healthcare companies and other large businesses, served largely from delivery centres in India.
exo: Exor is the Agnelli family's investment holding company, based in Amsterdam. It owns key stakes in Ferrari, Stellantis, CNH, Philips and Iveco, as well as the Juventus football club and The Economist.
exp: Eagle Materials is a US building materials maker based in Dallas, Texas. It produces cement, concrete, aggregates and gypsum wallboard, as well as recycled paperboard used to make that wallboard.
expd: Expeditors International is a US logistics company from Seattle, founded in 1979. It arranges international air and ocean freight, customs clearance and warehousing for companies without owning its own planes or ships.
expe: Expedia Group is an American online travel company from Seattle, founded in 1996 as a division of Microsoft. Through Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo people book hotels, flights, vacation rentals and rental cars.
expn: Experian is one of the world's largest credit bureaus, headquartered in Dublin. It collects credit histories of people and companies, calculates credit scores and sells data and analytics to lenders; in the US and UK consumers can also check their own score with it.
expo: Exponent is a US engineering and scientific consulting firm from Menlo Park, California. Its experts investigate accidents and product failures, assess product safety and health risks, and often serve as expert witnesses in court cases.
exr: Extra Space Storage is an American real estate investment trust (REIT) from Salt Lake City. It runs thousands of self-storage facilities where people and businesses rent units to keep their belongings.
ezj: easyJet is a British low-cost airline based at London Luton Airport, founded in 1995 by Stelios Haji-Ioannou. It flies short-haul routes across Europe from bases in the UK and the EU and also sells package trips through easyJet holidays.
f: Ford Motor Company is a US carmaker from Dearborn, Michigan, founded in 1903 by Henry Ford, who introduced assembly-line production. It builds F-Series pickups, Bronco and Explorer SUVs, the Mustang, Transit commercial vans and Lincoln cars.
f-token: SynFutures is a decentralized protocol for perpetual futures that lets users trade any asset and create new futures markets in seconds. Its V3 oAMM model combines an automated market maker with an on-chain order book; F is the protocol token.
f34: Wilmar International is a Singapore agribusiness group founded in 1991 by Kuok Khoon Hong and Martua Sitorus, and one of the world's largest processors and traders of palm oil. It also produces sugar, flour, rice and other foods, and sells consumer brands such as Arawana cooking oil in China.
faf: First American Financial is a California insurer with roots going back to 1889. It provides title insurance that protects property buyers and lenders, handles closing and escrow services for real estate deals, and offers property data.
fai: Freysa is an AI agent on the Base network, known for a game in which people paid to try to convince it to hand over a prize pool. The project builds autonomous AI agents that manage funds on their own; FAI is the ecosystem token.
falabella: Falabella is one of Latin America's largest retailers, based in Santiago and founded in 1889 as a tailor's shop. It runs Falabella department stores, Sodimac home-improvement stores, Tottus supermarkets, shopping malls through Mallplaza and Banco Falabella, mainly in Chile, Peru and Colombia.
fang: Diamondback Energy is a US oil and gas producer from Midland, Texas. It drills for oil and gas only in the Permian Basin of West Texas, the largest oil region in the United States.
fanuc: Fanuc is a Japanese factory automation company based at the foot of Mount Fuji, founded in 1972. It is the world leader in CNC controls for machine tools and also makes industrial robots and machine tools.
far: FAR Labs (FAR) is the team behind Farcana, a team-based multiplayer shooter game with Web3 features. The FAR token is used in its gaming ecosystem for rewards and in-game activity.
farm: Harvest Finance is a DeFi yield aggregator launched in 2020 that automatically moves deposits into farming strategies and reinvests the rewards. FARM is its token; holders can stake it to receive a share of the protocol's profits.
fartcoin: Fartcoin (FARTCOIN) is a meme coin on Solana that appeared in late 2024 out of jokes around the AI agent Truth Terminal. The token has no practical use and exists as an internet joke, so its price depends on community interest.
fast: Fastenal is a US industrial supplies distributor based in Winona, Minnesota, founded in 1967. It sells fasteners, tools and safety gear to factories and builders through a network of branches and vending machines placed right at customers' sites.
fast-retailing: Fast Retailing is a Japanese company from Yamaguchi that owns Uniqlo, Asia's largest clothing chain. It also runs the GU, Theory and Comptoir des Cotonniers brands; founder Tadashi Yanai turned a family shop into a global retailer of basic clothing.
fbin: Fortune Brands Innovations is a US home products maker based in Illinois. It owns Moen faucets, Master Lock padlocks, Therma-Tru entry doors and the House of Rohl luxury kitchen and bath brands.
fbk: FinecoBank is an Italian online bank and broker based in Milan, launched in 1999 within UniCredit and independent since 2019. It offers current accounts, trading on global markets, investment funds and financial advice through one digital platform.
fbomb: Fantom Bomb (fBOMB) is a decentralized finance token issued on several networks, including Fantom, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Arbitrum and Optimism. It is used in the project's DeFi pools and community apps.
fbtc: Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) is Fidelity's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024, which holds real bitcoin in Fidelity's own custody.
fbu: Fletcher Building is New Zealand's largest building materials and construction company, based in Auckland, with roots going back to 1909. It makes products such as GIB plasterboard, concrete, steel and Laminex surfaces, runs the PlaceMakers building supply stores, and builds homes and large infrastructure projects.
fcfs: FirstCash is a pawn store operator from Fort Worth, Texas, with thousands of shops in the United States, Mexico and Latin America. It makes small loans secured by personal items and sells pre-owned goods; it also offers lease-to-own payments through American First Finance.
fcn: FTI Consulting is a Washington, D.C., business advisory firm founded in 1982. It helps companies through crises, restructurings, litigation and investigations, and also offers economic consulting, technology and strategic communications services.
fct: FirmaChain (FCT) is a South Korean blockchain for electronic contracts. It lets people and companies sign, store and verify agreements and notarized documents on-chain, so the record cannot be forged or disputed; FCT pays for the network's services.
fcx: Freeport-McMoRan is a US mining company based in Phoenix, Arizona, and one of the world's largest copper producers. It runs Indonesia's Grasberg mine, one of the biggest copper and gold deposits on Earth, plus mines in the US and Peru.
