hive: Hive is a blockchain that split from Steem in 2020 after the community rejected Justin Sun's takeover of Steemit. It rewards authors and readers for content, transactions on the network carry no fees, and it hosts the social network PeakD and the game Splinterlands.
hkex: HKEX (Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing) operates the Hong Kong stock exchange, its futures market and clearing houses. It also owns the London Metal Exchange (LME), and the Stock Connect programme links it with the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges.
hl: Hecla Mining is an Idaho mining company founded in 1891 and the largest silver producer in the United States. It mines silver, gold, lead and zinc at mines in Alaska, Idaho and Canada.
hli: Houlihan Lokey is an American investment bank based in Los Angeles, founded in 1972. It advises companies on mergers and acquisitions and business valuations, and is regarded as one of the world's leading advisers on debt restructuring.
hlma: Halma is a British group based in Amersham that owns dozens of small technology companies. They make safety, environmental and healthcare products such as fire and gas detectors, water-quality sensors and medical and eye-care devices, sold worldwide.
hln: Haleon is a British consumer health company spun off from GSK in 2022. It makes Sensodyne and parodontax toothpaste, Panadol and Advil painkillers, Centrum vitamins and other over-the-counter products sold worldwide.
hln-token: Ēnosys (HLN) is a Web3 software house on the Flare Network that builds DeFi products such as a DEX, yield farming, interest-free loans and a cross-chain bridge, linked through its yield aggregator APYCloud. HLN is a governance token: holders stake it to create and vote on proposals.
hlne: Hamilton Lane is a Pennsylvania investment firm founded in 1991 that specialises in private markets. It invests money from pension funds, insurers, wealthy individuals and others in private equity, private credit, infrastructure and real estate funds.
hlt: Hilton Worldwide is a US hotel company based in McLean, Virginia, founded by Conrad Hilton in 1919. It manages and franchises thousands of hotels worldwide under brands such as Hilton, Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, DoubleTree and Hampton.
hm-b: H&M (Hennes & Mauritz) is a Swedish fashion retailer based in Stockholm, founded in 1947 by Erling Persson in Västerås. It sells affordable clothing, accessories and home goods in thousands of stores and online, and also owns COS, Weekday, Monki, & Other Stories and Arket.
hmm: Thinking Cat (HMM) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
hmnd: Humanode (HMND) is a layer-1 blockchain where every validator node must be a verified unique person, following the idea of one human, one node, one vote. Users prove they are real with a private face scan on their phone, and the network is built on Substrate and works with Ethereum tools.
hmstr: Hamster Kombat is a tap-to-earn game in Telegram where players run a virtual crypto exchange as a hamster CEO. It became one of the most-played Telegram games in 2024; HMSTR is its token, distributed to players in an airdrop on the TON blockchain.
hnfg: Henderson is a Russian chain of men's clothing stores based in Moscow, founded in 1993. It designs and sells suits, shirts, shoes and accessories under its own brand through hundreds of stores and online.
hnr1: Hannover Re is one of the world's largest reinsurers, based in Hanover, Germany, and founded in 1966. It insures other insurance companies against big risks such as natural catastrophes, as well as property, casualty, life and health policies; its majority owner is the German insurance group Talanx.
hnt: Helium (HNT) is a decentralized wireless network where people install hotspots and earn tokens for providing coverage. It first served IoT devices and now develops the Helium Mobile cellular service; since 2023 it has run on the Solana blockchain.
ho: Thales is a French defense and aerospace company from Paris. It makes radars, air defense systems, communications equipment, avionics and satellites, as well as cybersecurity and digital identity products such as SIM cards and passport chips.
hog: Harley-Davidson is the iconic American motorcycle maker from Milwaukee, founded in 1903. Besides heavy cruisers it sells parts, clothing and loans to buyers, and develops electric motorcycles under the LiveWire brand.
hogs: Lean hogs is a futures contract on the price of pork carcasses in the United States. It is driven by feed costs, exports to Asia and animal diseases.
hollar: HOLLAR (Hydrated Dollar) is a decentralized dollar stablecoin from Hydration, the DeFi network on Polkadot formerly known as HydraDX. Users mint HOLLAR by borrowing against crypto collateral in Hydration's money market.
holn: Holcim is a Swiss cement and building materials maker from Zug, founded in 1912 in the village of Holderbank. It produces cement, concrete, aggregates and roofing in dozens of countries; in 2025 it spun off its North American business as Amrize.
holo: Holoworld (HOLO) is a platform for creating AI-agent virtual characters without coding: they can chat, livestream and interact with people across social networks. The project is developed by the studio Hologram Labs, and HOLO is the ecosystem token.
homb: Home BancShares is a banking group from Conway, Arkansas, and the owner of Centennial Bank. It serves individuals, businesses and real estate developers in Arkansas, Florida, Texas, Alabama and New York.
home: HOME is the token of DeFi App, an app that brings trading, swaps and yield across different blockchains into one interface without gas or complex setup. HOME holders take part in governance and get benefits on the platform.
hon: Honeywell is a US industrial conglomerate headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with roots going back to the late 19th century. It makes avionics and aircraft engines, building and factory automation systems, sensors and industrial software.
hon-hai: Hon Hai Precision Industry, better known as Foxconn, is a Taiwanese company based in New Taipei, founded in 1974 by Terry Gou. It is the world's largest contract electronics maker, assembling iPhones and other devices for Apple and many brands, and builds AI servers.
hona: Honeywell Aerospace is a US maker of aviation and defense systems, separated from the Honeywell conglomerate into its own company. It produces avionics, radars, navigation and flight control systems, auxiliary power units and engines for planes, helicopters and spacecraft.
honda: Honda Motor is a Japanese car and motorcycle maker from Tokyo, founded by Soichiro Honda in 1948. It is the world's largest motorcycle maker and also builds Honda and Acura cars, engines, generators and the HondaJet business jet.
honey: HONEY is the token of Hivemapper, a decentralized mapping network on Solana. Drivers mount Hivemapper dashcams in their cars to collect street-level imagery for a constantly updated world map and earn HONEY for their contributions, while companies pay to use the map data.
hong-leong-bank: Hong Leong Bank is a Malaysian bank and part of the Hong Leong Group controlled by the Quek family. It provides retail and business banking and Islamic banking through Hong Leong Islamic Bank, and has operations in Singapore, Hong Kong, Vietnam and Cambodia plus a stake in China's Bank of Chengdu.
hood: Robinhood Markets is a US fintech company based in Menlo Park, California, founded in 2013. Its app popularised commission-free stock trading and also offers crypto and options trading, retirement accounts and credit cards.
hookr: Hookr.fun (HOOKR) is a token-launch platform on Robinhood Chain, the blockchain network started by the US trading app Robinhood. Anyone can create and trade new tokens there, and HOOKR is the platform's own token.
hoppy: Hoppy (HOPPY) is a meme token on Ethereum built around Hoppy, a frog character from Matt Furie's comic The Night Riders; Furie is also the creator of Pepe. The project is not officially linked to him, and the token has no utility beyond community and trading.
hopr: HOPR is a privacy protocol from Switzerland that runs a decentralized mixnet, hiding who is talking to whom when data moves across the internet. People who run HOPR nodes relay traffic and earn HOPR tokens for it.
hot: Holo (HOT) is the token of Holo, a project building hosting for apps on Holochain, a platform for distributed applications that does not use a classic blockchain. Computer owners can rent out space and processing power for hosting and earn rewards.
hot-de: Hochtief is a German construction group based in Essen and controlled by Spain's ACS. It builds infrastructure, offices and data centres mainly in the US through Turner, in Australia through CIMIC, and in Europe, and holds a stake in toll-road operator Abertis.
hoya: HOYA is a Japanese company from Tokyo, founded in 1941 as an optical glass maker. It makes eyeglass lenses, contact lenses, medical endoscopes (Pentax Medical), and photomasks and glass substrates for electronics.
hp: Hippo Protocol (HP) is a layer-1 blockchain built for healthcare. It aims to let patients and medical organizations store and share health data securely under the patient's control, and HP is the network's native token.
hpe: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is a US technology company based in Houston, spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 2015. It sells servers, data storage systems, Aruba and Juniper networking equipment and cloud services to businesses.
hpg: Hoa Phat Group is Vietnam's largest steel producer, founded in Hanoi in 1992. It makes construction rebar, hot-rolled coil and steel pipes at its Dung Quat complex, and also runs agriculture, home appliance and real estate businesses.
hpl: HyperLend (HPL) is the token of HyperLend, a decentralized lending and borrowing protocol on HyperEVM, the smart-contract layer of the Hyperliquid blockchain. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against their collateral.
hpp: House Party Protocol (HPP) is a Layer 2 blockchain network built for AI applications by the team behind Aergo from South Korea. Aergo tokens move to HPP, which is used to pay network fees, stake and vote.
hpq: HP Inc. is a US maker of laptops, PCs and printers from Palo Alto, successor to Hewlett-Packard, which was founded in a garage in 1939. It sells computers, printers and ink, HyperX gaming gear and Poly hybrid-work devices.
hqy: HealthEquity is an American company based in Utah and the largest administrator of health savings accounts (HSAs). Working through employers, it runs accounts that people use to pay for medical care and to invest savings tax-free.
hr: Healthcare Realty Trust is a Nashville REIT that owns medical office buildings, mostly located on or near major hospital campuses. It leases space to doctors' practices, outpatient clinics and health systems across the United States.
hrb: H&R Block is a Kansas City tax preparation company founded in 1955 by brothers Henry and Richard Bloch. It helps people and small businesses file tax returns through thousands of US offices and do-it-yourself software, and offers small-business banking via Wave.
hrho: EFG Holding, formerly EFG Hermes, is a Cairo-based financial group founded in 1984. It runs an investment bank active in brokerage, asset management and deal advisory across the Middle East, Africa and frontier markets, plus consumer finance (valU) and aiBANK.
hrl: Hormel Foods is a US food company from Austin, Minnesota, founded in 1891. It makes canned meat, bacon, nuts and ready meals, and its best-known brands include SPAM, Skippy peanut butter, Planters and Jennie-O turkey.
hsba: HSBC is one of the world's largest banks, headquartered in London and founded in 1865 in Hong Kong as the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. It earns most of its profit in Asia, serving individuals, companies and international trade.
hsbc-holdings: HSBC is a British-Asian banking group headquartered in London, founded in 1865 in Hong Kong as the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. One of the world's largest banks, it earns most of its profit in Asia, especially Hong Kong.
hsic: Henry Schein is an American distributor of dental and medical supplies based in Melville, New York, founded in 1932. It supplies dental and doctors' practices with materials, equipment, medicines and practice-management software.
hsk: HashKey Platform Token (HSK) is the ecosystem token of HashKey, a Hong Kong financial group that runs a licensed crypto exchange. It is used on the HashKey Chain network and to reward participants in the ecosystem.
hst: Host Hotels & Resorts is the largest US lodging real estate investment trust (REIT), based in Bethesda, Maryland, and was spun off from Marriott in 1993. It owns luxury and upper-upscale hotels run under brands such as Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, Hyatt, Hilton and Four Seasons.
hsy: The Hershey Company is an American maker of chocolate and sweets from Hershey, Pennsylvania, founded by Milton Hershey in 1894. It is known for Hershey's bars, Reese's, Kit Kat (in the US) and snacks such as SkinnyPop.
ht: Huobi Token (HT) is the exchange token of Huobi, a crypto exchange founded in Beijing in 2013 by Leon Li that renamed itself HTX in 2023. The token gave discounts on trading fees and access to exchange services.
htm: Hatom (HTM) is the token of Hatom, a DeFi protocol on the MultiversX blockchain. Its main products are a lending and borrowing market and liquid staking of EGLD; HTM is used for governance and rewards.
hto: OTE (Hellenic Telecommunications Organization) is Greece's largest telecoms company, based in Athens. Under the COSMOTE brand it provides mobile, fixed-line, broadband and TV services; Deutsche Telekom is its main shareholder.
htr: Hathor (HTR) is the coin of Hathor Network, a layer-1 blockchain that combines a DAG structure with a classic blockchain. It is known for letting anyone create tokens in a few clicks without writing smart contracts, and it is merge-mined with Bitcoin.
htx: HTX is the governance token of HTX DAO, the ecosystem around the HTX crypto exchange (formerly Huobi), which is linked to Justin Sun. Token holders vote on the project's development and get perks in the exchange's services.
hubb: Hubbell is a US maker of electrical equipment based in Connecticut, founded in 1888 by Harvey Hubbell, inventor of the detachable electric plug. It makes power-grid components, outlets, switches, lighting and wiring systems.
hubs: HubSpot is an American software company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2006. Its cloud CRM platform, with Marketing Hub, Sales Hub and Service Hub, helps small and mid-sized businesses attract customers, sell and support them.
huh1v: Huhtamäki is a Finnish food packaging maker based in Espoo, founded in 1920. It produces paper cups, food containers, egg cartons and flexible packaging used by restaurant chains, food brands and retailers around the world.
hum: Humana is a US health insurer from Louisville, Kentucky, founded in 1961. It is one of the largest providers of Medicare Advantage plans for older Americans and runs clinics, pharmacies and home care through CenterWell.
huma: Huma Finance is a PayFi network that provides liquidity for payments and receivables financing on blockchain, notably on Solana. It lets users earn from real-world payment flows; HUMA is the governance token.
hunt: HUNT is the token of Hunt Town, a South Korean team of builders behind Steemhunt and the Mint Club token-creation platform. On Mint Club anyone can launch tokens priced by a bonding curve, often using HUNT as the reserve asset.
hut: Hut 8 is a North American energy and digital infrastructure company, founded in Canada in 2017 and now based in Miami. It mines bitcoin, largely through its majority-owned American Bitcoin, and develops power sites and data centres for AI and high-performance computing.
hvlo: Hivello (HVLO) is the token of Hivello, a desktop app that lets ordinary computers run several DePIN networks at once, sharing spare resources and earning rewards without technical setup.
hwc: Hancock Whitney is a banking group based in Gulfport, Mississippi. Its bank serves individuals, small businesses and companies along the US Gulf Coast, in Mississippi, Louisiana, Alabama, Florida and Texas.
hwm: Howmet Aerospace is a US company based in Pittsburgh that makes engineered metal parts for aircraft engines and airframes, such as turbine blades, fasteners and structural components, plus forged aluminum wheels for trucks. It was spun out of Arconic, the former Alcoa, in 2020.
hxl: Hexcel is an advanced composites maker from Stamford, Connecticut. It produces carbon fibre, reinforcements, prepregs and honeycomb materials used to build lighter aircraft, helicopters, satellites and industrial products, with Airbus and Boeing among its main customers.
hydr: RusHydro is Russia's largest hydropower generator, controlled by the state. It runs dozens of hydroelectric plants, including the Sayano-Shushenskaya dam on the Yenisei, as well as power and heat plants across the Far East.
hype: Hyperliquid is its own layer-1 blockchain, best known for the decentralised exchange of the same name for perpetual futures and spot trading. HYPE is used for staking, fees and governance; the project is led by Jeff Yan.
hype3: Hypera Pharma is one of Brazil's largest pharmaceutical companies, based in São Paulo. It makes and sells over-the-counter brands such as Benegrip, Engov and Doril, plus prescription drugs, branded generics and skincare, mainly through Brazilian pharmacies.
hyper: Hyperlane is a permissionless interoperability protocol: anyone can connect their blockchain and send messages and tokens across dozens of networks. HYPER is the token for staking and governance.
hyundai-mobis: Hyundai Mobis is a South Korean auto parts maker from Seoul and a key company of Hyundai Motor Group. It produces chassis and cockpit modules, safety systems, electronics and electric-vehicle components, and supplies spare parts for Hyundai and Kia.
hyundai-motor: Hyundai Motor is South Korea's largest carmaker, headquartered in Seoul and founded in 1967. It builds Hyundai cars and the premium Genesis brand, ranks with Kia among the world's three largest car groups and owns Boston Dynamics.
iag: International Airlines Group (IAG) is an airline group based in London and Madrid, created in 2011 by the merger of British Airways and Iberia. It also owns Aer Lingus, Vueling and Level, flying across the Atlantic, within Europe and to Latin America.
iag-token: Iagon is a decentralized storage and computing platform built mainly on Cardano. People and businesses rent out spare disk space and processing power to the network, and the IAG token pays for these services and rewards providers.
ibe: Iberdrola is a Spanish energy company from Bilbao and one of the world's largest producers of wind and solar power. It owns power grids in Spain, the United Kingdom (ScottishPower), the United States (Avangrid) and Brazil (Neoenergia) and supplies electricity to millions of customers.
ibit: iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is BlackRock's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024. It lets investors own bitcoin through a regular brokerage account without a crypto wallet.
ibkr: Interactive Brokers is a US online broker based in Greenwich, Connecticut, founded by Thomas Peterffy. It gives access to stocks, options, futures, currencies and bonds on hundreds of exchanges in dozens of countries and is known for low fees for active traders.
ibm: IBM is an American technology company based in Armonk, New York, founded in 1911. Once a leader in mainframes and personal computers, it now sells Red Hat hybrid cloud, enterprise software, the watsonx AI platform and consulting, and develops quantum computers.
iboc: International Bancshares is a bank holding company from Laredo, Texas, on the Mexican border. Its main bank, International Bank of Commerce (IBC), serves people and businesses in Texas and Oklahoma with accounts, loans, mortgages and cross-border trade finance.
ibs: IBS is the algorithmic token of POTS Money, a modular DeFi protocol. IBS is not a stablecoin: it is minted through collateralized debt as users bond and stake, and the ecosystem adds payments, lending, auctions and AI tools for yield strategies.
ibs-pt: Ibersol is a Portuguese restaurant operator based in Porto. It runs franchised fast-food chains such as KFC and Pizza Hut in Portugal and Spain, plus its own brands and catering at airports and motorway service areas.
ibvm: IBVM (International Bitcoin Virtual Machine) is a Bitcoin layer-2 network built as an EVM-compatible ZK rollup, adding smart contracts and DeFi to Bitcoin without changing its base layer. The IBVM token pays network fees and is used for staking and governance.
icbc: ICBC (Industrial and Commercial Bank of China) is a state-owned Chinese bank based in Beijing and one of the largest banks in the world by assets. Founded in 1984, it serves hundreds of millions of customers and large companies; its H shares trade in Hong Kong.
icbc-cn: ICBC (A shares) are shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The state-owned Beijing bank, founded in 1984, is one of the world's largest and serves individuals, companies and the government through thousands of branches.
icbp: Indofood CBP is a Jakarta-based maker of branded packaged foods and part of the Salim group's Indofood. Its best-known product is Indomie instant noodles, sold in dozens of countries; it also makes dairy products, snacks, seasonings and drinks.
ice: Intercontinental Exchange is a US operator of exchanges and financial data based in Atlanta, founded in 2000 by Jeffrey Sprecher. It owns the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the ICE futures exchanges, and provides mortgage technology and data services.
icicibank: ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private-sector banks, based in Mumbai and founded in 1994. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, and through subsidiaries also insurance and asset management.
icl: ICL Group, formerly Israel Chemicals, is a Tel Aviv-based specialty minerals and fertiliser company. It extracts potash and bromine from the Dead Sea and mines phosphate, turning them into fertilisers, flame retardants, food additives and industrial chemicals sold worldwide.
icln: iShares Global Clean Energy (ICLN) invests worldwide in solar, wind and other clean-energy companies.
icnt: Impossible Cloud Network (ICNT) is a decentralized protocol for business cloud services: storage, compute and networking. Hardware owners contribute resources and service providers use them; ICNT is needed for node collateral, access to resources and staking.
icp: Internet Computer is a blockchain from the Swiss DFINITY Foundation (Zurich), founded by Dominic Williams, launched in 2021. The network lets websites, services and AI agents run entirely on-chain without ordinary cloud servers; ICP pays for computation.
icx: ICON is a South Korean blockchain project launched in 2017–2018 with the goal of connecting separate blockchains so they can exchange data and value, and it later built cross-chain messaging tools for other networks. ICX is the network's coin, used for fees, staking and governance.
id: SPACE ID (ID) is a universal domain name service for Web3: users register and trade domains such as .bnb or .arb that replace long wallet addresses. The project was backed by Binance Labs, and ID is its governance token.
ida: IDACORP is an American utility holding company based in Boise, Idaho. Its subsidiary Idaho Power generates and delivers electricity to homes and businesses in southern Idaho and eastern Oregon, much of it from hydroelectric dams on the Snake River.
idcc: InterDigital is a research and development company from Wilmington, Delaware, that invents wireless and video technologies. It licenses its patents behind 4G, 5G, Wi-Fi and video coding to smartphone, TV and consumer-electronics makers.
idle: IdleMine (IDLE) is the token of a play-to-earn mobile game where players hold a thumb on the screen to mine rewards, fight 1v1 battles against others, and collect daily login bonuses and loot crates.
idol: MEET48 (IDOL) is a Web3 entertainment platform about virtual and real idols that combines AI, live streaming and game mechanics. Fans support their favorite performers and take part in shows, and the IDOL token serves as the ecosystem's currency.
idr: Indra is a Spanish technology company based in Madrid that specialises in defence, air traffic management and IT. It builds radars, air traffic control systems and military electronics, and runs digital services through its subsidiary Minsait; the Spanish state holding SEPI is a key shareholder.
idxx: IDEXX Laboratories is a US company from Westbrook, Maine, founded in 1983. It is the world leader in veterinary diagnostics, making analyzers and tests for clinics that treat cats and dogs, plus tests for livestock, milk and drinking water.
iesc: IES Holdings is a Houston company that designs and installs electrical and technology systems. It works on data centres, commercial and industrial buildings and homes, and also makes electrical equipment such as switchgear and generator enclosures.
iex: IDEX Corporation is a US industrial company from Northbrook, Illinois, founded in 1988. It makes specialized pumps, flow meters, fluidics for lab and medical instruments, fire and rescue equipment such as the Hurst Jaws of Life, and precision optics.
ifc: Intact Financial is Canada's largest property and casualty insurer, headquartered in Toronto. It insures cars, homes and businesses and also operates in the United States, the United Kingdom and Ireland.
iff: International Flavors & Fragrances (IFF) is a New York-based company whose roots go back to 1889. It creates flavors and scents for food, drinks, perfumes and household products, and also makes food ingredients, enzymes and probiotics.
ift: Infratil is a New Zealand infrastructure investment company that owns stakes in long-term assets in New Zealand, Australia, the US and Europe. Its main holdings include CDC Data Centres in Australia, telecom operator One NZ, renewable energy developers and Wellington Airport.
ifx: Infineon Technologies is Germany's largest chipmaker, based in Neubiberg near Munich and spun off from Siemens in 1999. It makes power chips and microcontrollers for cars, electric vehicles, solar inverters, industry and bank cards.
ihg: InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG) is a British hotel company that franchises and manages thousands of hotels worldwide. Its brands include Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, InterContinental, Crowne Plaza and Kimpton, and it runs the IHG One Rewards loyalty programme.
ihh-healthcare: IHH Healthcare is a Malaysian hospital group based in Kuala Lumpur and one of the world's largest private healthcare providers. It runs hospitals and clinics under brands such as Mount Elizabeth and Gleneagles in Singapore, Pantai in Malaysia, Acıbadem in Turkey and Fortis in India.
ihi: IHI is a Japanese heavy-industry company headquartered in Tokyo, whose roots go back to the Ishikawajima shipyard founded in 1853. It makes jet-engine parts, turbochargers, boilers and power equipment, bridges and industrial machinery, and works on rocket and space systems.
iii: 3i Group is a British investment company based in London, founded in 1945, that invests in private companies and infrastructure. Its largest holding is Action, the European discount retail chain.
ika: Ika (IKA) is a fast multi-party computation (MPC) network built on Sui. Its 'dWallets' let apps control assets on other blockchains, such as Bitcoin, without bridges; IKA is used for fees and staking.
ilmn: Illumina is an American company from San Diego and the world leader in DNA sequencing technology. Labs, hospitals and scientists use its instruments and reagents to read genomes, diagnose cancer and run genetic research.
ilv: Illuvium is an open-world Web3 game where players explore a planet, capture creatures called Illuvials and battle in an auto-battler. The project was founded by brothers Kieran and Aaron Warwick; ILV is used for governance and rewards.
imb: Imperial Brands is a British tobacco company based in Bristol. It sells cigarettes and tobacco under brands such as Davidoff, West, JPS and Gauloises, plus blu e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches.
imc: IMC (Industrial Milk Company) is a Ukrainian agricultural group operating in the Poltava, Chernihiv and Sumy regions, with shares listed in Warsaw. It grows corn, sunflower and wheat, and runs its own grain elevators and a dairy farm.
imcd: IMCD is a Dutch distributor of speciality chemicals and ingredients based in Rotterdam. It supplies components for cosmetics, food, pharmaceuticals, coatings and plastics to manufacturers in dozens of countries, backed by technical labs.
imo: IMO is the token of a real-estate investment project that aims to let anyone earn monthly passive income from property, whatever the amount invested. Income from the properties the company owns is shared with token holders.
imu: Immunefi (IMU) is the token of Immunefi, a leading bug bounty and security platform for Web3. Projects pay security researchers through it for finding vulnerabilities in their smart contracts before hackers do.
imx: Immutable (IMX) is a blockchain gaming platform from Sydney, Australia, that runs the Ethereum layer-2 networks Immutable X and Immutable zkEVM. They let players trade in-game NFTs without paying gas fees; IMX is used for fees, staking and governance.
in: INFINIT is an AI-powered DeFi intelligence protocol that lets anyone discover, compare and execute DeFi opportunities through AI agents and plain-language requests instead of navigating many apps by hand. IN is the protocol's token.
inc: WorldAssets (INC) is an Ethereum-based DeFi project focused on real-world assets (RWA): it aims to bring traditional assets on-chain as tokens that can be held and traded like crypto.
incb: Incab is a Russian cable manufacturer based in Perm. It makes fibre-optic cables for telecoms and power lines as well as other communication cables, and exports to many countries.
incy: Incyte is a US biopharmaceutical company from Delaware. It develops medicines for blood cancers and inflammatory and autoimmune diseases; its main drug is Jakafi (ruxolitinib), and it also sells Opzelura cream for vitiligo and eczema.
index: INDEX is the governance token of Index Coop, a community that creates crypto index and strategy tokens such as the DeFi Pulse Index (DPI). Holders vote on new products, fees and how the treasury is used.
indf: Indofood Sukses Makmur is an Indonesian food group based in Jakarta and part of the Salim Group. It owns the flour miller Bogasari, the Indomie noodle maker Indofood CBP, oil palm plantations and a large distribution network.
indigo: IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is India's largest airline by passengers, a low-cost carrier based in Gurugram that started flying in 2006. It runs a large fleet of Airbus A320-family jets on domestic routes and a growing number of international flights.
indy: Indigo Protocol (INDY) is the governance token of Indigo, a DeFi protocol on Cardano for synthetic assets called iAssets, such as iUSD and iBTC. Users mint iAssets against ADA collateral, and INDY holders vote on the protocol.
inf: Informa is a London-based British company and the world's largest organiser of business trade shows and conferences. It also publishes academic books and journals through Taylor & Francis and provides B2B data and digital services.
infi: infiniFi is an on-chain banking protocol with dollar yield products: deposits are spread across strategies of different durations, similar to how banks manage assets and liabilities. INFI is the protocol's token.
infy: Infosys is an Indian IT company from Bengaluru, founded in 1981 by seven engineers led by N. R. Narayana Murthy. It provides software development, digital transformation, cloud and consulting services to large companies worldwide.
ing: ING Bank Śląski is one of Poland's largest banks, based in Katowice and part of the Dutch ING Group. It offers everyday banking, loans, savings, investments and corporate services to individuals and businesses across Poland and is known for its mobile and online banking.
inga: ING Group is a Dutch banking group headquartered in Amsterdam, formed in 1991. It serves millions of retail customers across Europe and beyond, known for its digital-first banking, and also provides wholesale banking to large companies.
ingr: Ingredion is a US ingredients company based in Westchester, Illinois, formerly called Corn Products International. It turns corn, tapioca, potatoes and other plants into starches, sweeteners and texturizers used in food, drinks and industrial products.
init: Initia is a blockchain network that joins many optimistic rollups into one interconnected system. Developers launch their own app-specific chains that can easily talk to each other; INIT is used for staking and governance.
inj: Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK for financial apps such as exchanges, derivatives and tokenized assets. It gives developers ready-made trading modules; INJ is used for staking, governance and paying network fees.
inpst: InPost is a Polish logistics company founded in Kraków and registered in Luxembourg. It runs Poland's largest network of parcel lockers (Paczkomaty) for online shoppers and is expanding the model across Europe, including the UK, France and Italy.
insm: Insmed is a US biopharmaceutical company from New Jersey. It develops medicines for rare lung diseases, including the inhaled antibiotic Arikayce and brensocatib for bronchiectasis.
intc: Intel is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1968 by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore. It is known for Core and Xeon processors for PCs and servers and is building a contract chip-manufacturing business, Intel Foundry.
intc-token: Intel • Robinhood Token is a tokenized version of Intel shares issued by Robinhood for its customers in the European Union. It follows the price of the US-listed stock and can be traded around the clock on a blockchain.
inter: Inter Milan Fan Token (INTER) is the official fan token of FC Internazionale Milano, the Italian football club founded in 1908. Issued on the Chiliz blockchain via the Socios.com app, it lets fans vote in club polls and get rewards and experiences.
intu: Intuit is a US financial software company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 1983. It makes TurboTax for filing taxes, QuickBooks accounting for small businesses, the Credit Karma personal finance app and the Mailchimp email marketing service.
inv: Inverse Finance (INV) is the governance token of Inverse Finance, a DeFi project on Ethereum that issues the DOLA stablecoin and runs FiRM, a lending market with fixed borrowing rates. INV holders vote on the protocol and can stake it.
inve-b: Investor AB is the Wallenberg family's investment company in Stockholm, founded in 1916. It holds large long-term stakes in Nordic companies such as Atlas Copco, ABB, AstraZeneca, SEB, Ericsson and Saab, and owns private firms through Patricia Industries.
invh: Invitation Homes is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from Dallas and the largest owner of single-family rental homes in the country. Founded by Blackstone in 2012, it rents and manages houses mainly in fast-growing Sun Belt and West Coast markets.
inx: Infinex (INX) is the token of Infinex, a crypto platform founded by Synthetix creator Kain Warwick. It aims to feel as simple as a centralized exchange while users keep control of their own funds across many blockchains.
io: io.net (IO) is a decentralized GPU network on Solana that pools graphics cards from data centers, mining farms and private computers into clusters for machine learning. AI engineers rent computing power for less than in regular clouds; IO is used for payments and rewards.
ioi-corporation: IOI Corporation is a Malaysian palm oil company based in Putrajaya. It runs oil palm plantations in Malaysia and Indonesia and, through its resource-based manufacturing arm, refines palm oil and makes oleochemicals used in food, soaps and cosmetics.
ion: Ice Open Network (ION) is the coin of ION, a layer-1 blockchain built on technology from TON that grew out of the Ice Network mobile "mining" app launched in 2023. The project focuses on decentralised social and content apps such as Online+.
ionq: IonQ is a US quantum computing company from Maryland that builds quantum computers based on trapped ions. It offers access to its machines through the AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud clouds and also develops quantum networking and sensing.
iost: IOST is a high-throughput blockchain platform launched in 2019 by a team backed by Sequoia and Matrix. It uses its own Proof of Believability consensus and focuses on fast, cheap decentralized apps.
iot: Samsara is a US technology company from San Francisco, founded in 2015, that sells its 'Connected Operations' cloud platform. Trucking fleets, construction firms and other physical-operations businesses use its sensors, AI dashcams and software to track vehicles, improve driver safety and cut fuel costs.
iota: IOTA is an open-source blockchain project run by the Berlin-based IOTA Foundation and founded in 2015. Originally built for the Internet of Things, it now focuses on digital identity, trade data and tokenization; the IOTA token pays fees and is used for staking.
iotx: IoTeX is a blockchain platform launched in 2017 that connects real-world devices to blockchain and AI. It feeds verified data from sensors, cars and gadgets into decentralized apps and develops the DePIN sector; IOTX is the network's native coin.
ip: International Paper is a US packaging maker based in Memphis, Tennessee, founded in 1898 and one of the world's largest producers of paper-based packaging. It makes containerboard and corrugated boxes for e-commerce, food and industry, and bought Britain's DS Smith in 2025.
ipgp: IPG Photonics is a US maker of fiber lasers based in Marlborough, Massachusetts, founded in 1990 by physicist Valentin Gapontsev. Its lasers are used mainly to cut, weld and mark metal in factories, and also in medicine and research.
iq: IQ is the token of IQ.wiki (formerly Everipedia), the largest blockchain-based encyclopedia about crypto. The project also develops AI agents through its IQ AI platform, and the token is used for governance and rewards for editors.
iqv: IQVIA is a US company from North Carolina that runs clinical trials of new medicines for pharmaceutical companies and sells healthcare data and analytics. It was formed in 2016 by the merger of Quintiles and IMS Health.
ir: Ingersoll Rand is an American industrial equipment maker from Davidson, North Carolina, with a history dating to the 19th century. It makes compressors, vacuum pumps, blowers and fluid-handling systems for factories, healthcare and energy.
ir-token: Infrared Finance (IR) is the governance token of Infrared, the liquid staking and proof-of-liquidity protocol on Berachain. Staking IR gives sIR, which earns a share of protocol fees and voting power.
ir5b: Irish Continental Group is an Irish shipping and transport company based in Dublin. It runs Irish Ferries passenger and freight services between Ireland, Britain and France, and container shipping and terminals through Eucon and its Dublin and Belfast port operations.
irao: Inter RAO is a Russian state-controlled power company based in Moscow. It owns large power plants, sells electricity to end consumers through retail supply companies, and handles electricity exports and imports.
irctc: IRCTC (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) is a state-owned company under India's Ministry of Railways. It runs the official online train-ticket booking platform, provides catering on trains and at stations, sells Rail Neer bottled water and offers tour packages.
iren: IREN (formerly Iris Energy) is a data-center company from Sydney, Australia, listed in the US. It owns large sites powered by renewable energy in Texas and British Columbia, where it mines bitcoin and increasingly rents out GPU capacity for AI cloud computing.
ires: Irish Residential Properties REIT (I-RES) is a Dublin-based real estate investment trust. It owns and rents out several thousand modern apartments, mainly in and around Dublin, to private tenants.
irkt: Yakovlev (formerly Irkut Corporation) is a Russian aircraft maker within the state United Aircraft Corporation. It develops the MC-21 airliner and SJ-100 regional jet, builds Su-30 fighters at its Irkutsk plant and makes the Yak-130 trainer.
irm: Iron Mountain is an American real estate investment trust (REIT) from Boston, founded in 1951. It stores paper archives and records for thousands of companies in dozens of countries, shreds confidential documents and also builds and leases data centers.
irsa: IRSA is Argentina's largest real estate company, based in Buenos Aires and controlled by the agribusiness group Cresud. It owns and runs shopping malls such as Alto Palermo and Abasto, premium office buildings and hotels including the Llao Llao in Bariloche, and develops large urban projects.
irt: Independence Realty Trust is a US real estate investment trust based in Philadelphia that owns and runs apartment communities. It focuses on mid-sized, fast-growing cities in the Sun Belt and Midwest rather than the most expensive coastal markets.
irys: Irys (IRYS) is a layer-1 blockchain that combines data storage with smart-contract execution, formerly known as Bundlr. It is designed for large volumes of data for AI and Web3 applications.
isctr: İş Bankası (Türkiye İş Bankası) is one of Turkey's largest private banks, founded in 1924 on the initiative of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. It serves millions of customers through a wide branch network and holds stakes in many Turkish companies.
islm: Islamic Coin (ISLM) is the native coin of the HAQQ network, an Ethereum-compatible blockchain from Dubai designed to follow Sharia principles. Part of newly issued coins goes to the Evergreen DAO, which funds Islamic charity and community projects.
ismen: İş Yatırım is a Turkish investment bank and brokerage based in Istanbul, founded in 1996 and part of the İşbank group. It offers share and derivatives trading, investment banking, research and asset management.
isp: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest bank, formed in 2007 by the merger of Banca Intesa and Sanpaolo IMI and headquartered in Turin. It serves millions of customers in Italy and Central and Eastern Europe and runs a large insurance and asset management business.
isrg: Intuitive Surgical is a California company founded in 1995 and a pioneer of robotic surgery. Its da Vinci system lets surgeons perform minimally invasive operations with robotic arms; the company earns money from instruments and service.
iss: ISS is a Danish facility services company based near Copenhagen, founded in 1901 and one of the world's largest private employers. It provides cleaning, workplace and food services, property maintenance and security to companies, hospitals and public institutions in dozens of countries.
it: Gartner is a US research and advisory company from Stamford, Connecticut, founded in 1979. It sells research and advice to IT and business leaders, runs large industry conferences and is known for its Magic Quadrant vendor rankings.
ita: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense (ITA) invests in American defence contractors and aerospace companies that build aircraft, missiles and space systems.
itc: ITC is an Indian conglomerate based in Kolkata, founded in 1910 as the Imperial Tobacco Company of India. It is the country's largest cigarette maker (Gold Flake, Classic) and a big packaged-foods company with brands such as Aashirvaad flour, Sunfeast biscuits and Bingo! snacks, and it also makes paperboard and packaging and runs agri-business.
ithaca: Ithaca Protocol (ITHACA) is the token of a non-custodial options protocol on Arbitrum whose auction-based matching engine handles vanilla options, digital options and structured products. The token launched in December 2024; early backers include Cumberland and Wintermute.
itochu: Itochu is a Japanese trading house based in Tokyo and Osaka, founded in 1858 as a textile merchant. It trades and invests in apparel, food, natural resources, machinery and retail, and owns the FamilyMart convenience store chain.
itrk: Intertek is a British testing, inspection and certification company based in London. It checks the quality and safety of consumer products, chemicals, oil and minerals, buildings and supply chains for manufacturers, retailers and governments in more than 100 countries.
itsa4: Itaúsa is a Brazilian holding company from São Paulo and the largest shareholder of the bank Itaú Unibanco. It also holds stakes in Alpargatas (Havaianas), Dexco, NTS gas pipelines, Copa Energia and Motiva (formerly CCR).
itt: ITT is a US industrial manufacturer based in Stamford, Connecticut, in its current form since a 2011 split of the old ITT Corporation. It makes brake pads and KONI shock absorbers for vehicles and trains, industrial pumps and valves, and connectors for aerospace, defense and industry.
itub4: Itaú Unibanco is the largest private bank in Brazil and Latin America, headquartered in São Paulo and formed in 2008 by the merger of Itaú and Unibanco. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, credit cards, insurance and asset management.
itw: Illinois Tool Works is a US industrial manufacturer based in Glenview, Illinois, founded in 1912. It runs seven businesses, from car components and welding equipment to commercial kitchen equipment, construction fasteners and polymers.
itx: Inditex is a Spanish fashion giant from Galicia founded by Amancio Ortega, owner of the chains Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius and Oysho. It is known for fast fashion: new collections reach thousands of stores worldwide within weeks.
ivat: IVA Technologies is a Russian software company based in Moscow that develops the IVA MCU video-conferencing platform. It also makes communication software and conference-room hardware for companies and government agencies.
ivg: Iveco Group is an Italian maker of trucks, buses and commercial vehicles based in Turin, spun off from CNH Industrial in 2022. Its brands include Iveco vans and trucks, FPT Industrial engines and Heuliez Bus.
ivl: Indorama Ventures is a Thai chemicals company from Bangkok, founded in 1994 by Aloke Lohia. It is the world's largest producer of PET resin for plastic bottles and also makes polyester fibres, with plants in dozens of countries.
ivv: iShares Core S&P 500 (IVV) is BlackRock's low-cost ETF on the S&P 500 index and one of the largest ETFs in the world.
ivz: Invesco is a US investment manager based in Atlanta that runs mutual funds and ETFs. It is known for the Invesco QQQ fund, which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index and is one of the most popular ETFs in the world.
iwm: iShares Russell 2000 (IWM) tracks the Russell 2000 index of small US companies. It is more sensitive to the economy and interest rates than the S&P 500.
ixs: IXS is the token of IX Swap, a platform for tokenized real-world assets and security tokens. Companies raise capital through its launchpad, and investors buy and trade tokenized shares, real estate and other assets after identity checks.
izi: iZUMi Finance (IZI) is the token of iZUMi, a multi-chain DeFi liquidity protocol whose main product iZiSwap is a decentralised exchange with discretised concentrated liquidity on networks such as BNB Chain, Ethereum layer 2s and others.
j: Jacobs Solutions is a US engineering and consulting firm based in Dallas, founded in 1947. It plans, designs and manages infrastructure projects such as water systems, transport and energy, as well as advanced facilities like data centers and pharmaceutical plants.
jagent: JAGENT is a token on BNB Chain from the Jager project (jager.live), focused on AI agents — software bots that perform tasks automatically. It belongs to the Jager community ecosystem alongside the Jager Hunter meme coin.
jager: Jager Hunter (JAGER) is a meme coin on BNB Chain. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
japan-post-holdings: Japan Post Holdings is the state-controlled parent of Japan's postal group, based in Tokyo and listed since its 2015 privatisation IPO. It runs the national mail and parcel service and post offices, and owns stakes in Japan Post Bank and Japan Post Insurance.
japan-tobacco: Japan Tobacco (JT) is a Tokyo-based tobacco maker and one of the largest in the world. Through JT International it sells Winston, Camel, Mevius and LD cigarettes and Ploom heated-tobacco products, and it also has pharmaceutical and food businesses.
jasmy: JasmyCoin is the token of Jasmy, a Tokyo-based Japanese company founded by former Sony executives. Jasmy builds an Internet of Things platform where users keep control of their own personal data; JASMY is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum.
jazz: Jazz Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland, founded in 2003. It focuses on sleep disorders, epilepsy and cancer, with medicines such as Xywav for narcolepsy, Epidiolex for rare epilepsies and Rylaze for leukemia.
jbht: J.B. Hunt Transport Services is one of the largest US freight companies, based in Lowell, Arkansas, and founded in 1961 by Johnnie Bryan Hunt. It is best known for intermodal shipping (containers moved by rail and truck) and also runs dedicated truck fleets and home delivery of bulky goods.
jbl: Jabil is a US contract electronics manufacturer from St. Petersburg, Florida, founded in 1966. It builds products for other brands, including data-centre hardware, smartphone components, medical devices, car electronics and packaging.
jci: Johnson Controls is a global company headquartered in Cork, Ireland, whose story began in the US in 1885 when Warren Johnson invented the electric thermostat. It makes heating, ventilation and air-conditioning, fire and security systems and smart-building software.
jct: Janction is a platform for sharing resources for AI products: GPU computing power, storage and images. Users can rent or lease out these resources, and the JCT token is used for settlements in the network.
jd: JD Sports Fashion is a British sports-fashion retailer founded in 1981 and based near Manchester. It sells trainers and sportswear from brands such as Nike and adidas through thousands of stores and online in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
jd-com: JD.com is a Chinese e-commerce company from Beijing, founded in 1998 by Liu Qiangdong (Richard Liu). It sells electronics, appliances and everyday goods and runs its own logistics network, JD Logistics, with warehouses and delivery across China.
jeanphil: Jean Phil (JEANPHIL) is a meme token on Solana tied to "Jean Phil", an AI-generated social media character with short videos on X, TikTok and Instagram. It launched on Pump.fun and is driven purely by community and online attention.
jef: Jefferies Financial Group is an American investment bank based in New York, founded in 1962 by Boyd Jefferies. It advises companies on mergers and acquisitions, helps them raise money by issuing shares and bonds, and trades securities for institutional clients.
jellyjelly: Jelly-My-Jelly (JELLYJELLY) is a meme token on Solana linked to the video app JellyJelly, created by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The token became a symbol of the app's community and trades as a meme asset.
jepi: JPMorgan Equity Premium Income (JEPI) holds S&P 500 stocks and sells options on them to pay a high monthly income, giving up part of the upside in return.
jepq: JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income (JEPQ) holds Nasdaq-100 stocks and sells options to fund monthly payouts, trading some growth for income.
jett: JETT is a cryptocurrency project that presents itself as a way to decentralize finance and give users more control over their money, with the stated goal of supporting space exploration efforts.
jetton: JetTon Games (JETTON) is the token of JetTon, a Telegram-based crypto casino in the TON ecosystem offering slots, live dealer games, crash games and sports betting. The operator holds an Anjouan gaming licence.
jeur: Jarvis Synthetic Euro (jEUR) is a synthetic stablecoin from Jarvis Network designed to track the value of one euro. It is minted against USDC collateral and is used mainly in decentralized finance on networks such as Polygon for euro payments, swaps and lending.
jhx: James Hardie Industries is a building materials company founded in Australia in 1888 and now registered in Ireland. It is the world's leading maker of fiber cement siding and backer board, sold mostly in North America under the Hardie brand.
jiangsu-hengrui: Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine is one of China's largest drugmakers, based in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province. It makes medicines for cancer, anesthesia and cardiovascular disease and actively develops its own innovative drugs.
jiofin: Jio Financial Services is an Indian financial company from Mumbai, spun off from Reliance Industries in 2023. It runs lending, payments, insurance broking and leasing businesses under the Jio brand and has an asset management joint venture with BlackRock.
jkhy: Jack Henry & Associates is a US fintech company from Missouri, founded in 1976. It builds software for community banks and credit unions: core account systems, online and mobile banking, and payment and card processing.
jll: JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle) is a global commercial real estate services firm headquartered in Chicago, formed in 1999 by the merger of Jones Lang Wootton and LaSalle Partners. It helps companies and investors lease, buy, sell and manage offices, warehouses and other property, and runs the investment manager LaSalle.
jmpt: JumpToken (JMPT) is the token of JumpTask, an online gig marketplace where companies post small tasks and people around the world complete them for crypto payments, including those without a bank account. The token runs on BNB Chain.
jmt: Jerónimo Martins is a Portuguese food retailer from Lisbon, founded in 1792. It runs Biedronka, Poland's largest supermarket chain, Pingo Doce in Portugal and Ara discount stores in Colombia.
jnj: Johnson & Johnson is a US healthcare company based in New Brunswick, New Jersey, founded in 1886. It develops prescription drugs for oncology, immunology and neuroscience, plus medical devices for surgery and cardiology; its consumer brands were spun off as Kenvue in 2023.
jnos: Slavneft-YANOS runs the oil refinery in Yaroslavl, one of the largest in central Russia, dating back to the Soviet era. It turns crude oil into petrol, diesel, jet fuel and bitumen and is controlled by Gazprom Neft and Rosneft through Slavneft.
jobcoin: JobCoin (JOBCOIN) is a memecoin on Solana built around the joke of escaping the 9-to-5 job and retiring early thanks to crypto. It has no product: its value rests on workplace-humor memes and an active community.
joby: Joby Aviation is a US company from Santa Cruz, California, founded in 2009 by JoeBen Bevirt. It is developing a quiet, piloted electric air taxi (eVTOL) that carries four passengers, with Toyota as a major investor and Delta Air Lines as a partner.
joe: JOE is the token of LFJ (formerly Trader Joe), a decentralized exchange running on Avalanche, Arbitrum and BNB Chain. The exchange is known for its Liquidity Book liquidity model; JOE is used for staking and governance.
joff: Chomolon Joff (JOFF) is a community meme coin from the Hyperliquid ecosystem. It celebrates the culture of fast-moving on-chain traders and positions itself as a symbol of the Hyperliquid movement, without venture-capital backing.
jpm: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank, headquartered in New York, with roots going back to 1799. It serves millions of customers under the Chase brand and runs investment banking, asset management and payments for big companies; it is led by Jamie Dimon.
jpyc: JPY Coin (JPYC) is a Japanese yen stablecoin from Tokyo-based JPYC Inc. Each token is designed to be worth one yen and redeemable for yen, and it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum, Polygon and Avalanche.
jr-east: JR East (East Japan Railway Company) is Japan's largest railway operator, based in Tokyo and created in 1987 when Japanese National Railways was privatised. It runs Tokyo commuter lines such as the Yamanote Line and Shinkansen routes to northern Japan, issues the Suica card and operates shops and hotels at its stations.
jst: JUST (JST) is the governance token of the JUST decentralized finance ecosystem on the TRON blockchain, linked to Justin Sun. The platform includes the JustLend lending service and stablecoin tools, and JST holders vote on protocol settings.
jsw: JSW (Jastrzębska Spółka Węglowa) is the European Union's largest producer of coking coal, based in Jastrzębie-Zdrój. It mines coal in Upper Silesia and makes coke for steelworks; the Polish state holds a controlling stake.
jswsteel: JSW Steel is one of India's largest steelmakers, based in Mumbai and the flagship of Sajjan Jindal's JSW Group. It produces hot-rolled, cold-rolled, galvanized and long steel products for construction, cars and industry.
jto: JTO is the governance token of Jito Network, a key piece of Solana infrastructure. Jito offers liquid staking of SOL through the JitoSOL token and a modified validator client that lets validators and stakers earn extra income from MEV.
jufo: Juhayna Food Industries is a leading Egyptian maker of dairy products and juices, founded in 1983 and based in Giza. Under the Juhayna brand and others it sells milk, yogurt, cooking dairy and fruit juices across Egypt.
juggernaut: The Juggernaut (JUGGERNAUT) is a meme token on Robinhood Chain, the Ethereum layer-2 network built by Robinhood. In September 2026 Robinhood added an information page for it in its app, which drew attention, though the token trades only on decentralized exchanges.
jup: Jupiter is the largest token-swap aggregator on Solana: it searches across decentralized exchanges for the best rate. It also offers perpetual futures, limit orders and new token launches; JUP is the governance token.
juv: Juventus Fan Token (JUV) is the fan token of Italian football club Juventus of Turin on the Socios.com platform (Chiliz blockchain). Holders vote in club polls, take part in quizzes and earn rewards.
jysk: Jyske Bank is one of Denmark's largest banks, based in Silkeborg in Jutland. It serves personal and business customers with everyday banking, loans, investments and pensions, and owns the mortgage lender Jyske Realkredit.
kag: Kinesis Silver (KAG) is a silver-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one troy ounce of investment-grade silver held in insured vaults. It can be spent, transferred or redeemed, and holders receive a share of platform fees.
kaia: Kaia is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain formed in 2024 by merging the Klaytn (from Kakao) and Finschia (from LINE) networks. It aims to bring Web3 to millions of users in Asia directly inside the KakaoTalk and LINE messengers; KAIA is its native coin.
kaio: KAIO (formerly Libre Capital) is a platform for tokenizing institutional funds: it issues on-chain shares of funds from large asset managers, opening them up to crypto investors. The project runs on networks including Hedera and has received funding from Tether; KAIO is the governance token.
kaito: KAITO is the token of Kaito, a platform that uses AI to collect and analyze crypto news, social media and discussions. Its InfoFi network rewards content creators and researchers for the attention they attract; KAITO is used for rewards, staking and governance.
kakao: Kakao is a South Korean internet company based on Jeju Island, best known for KakaoTalk, the messenger used by almost everyone in the country. Around it Kakao has built an ecosystem of KakaoBank, Kakao Pay, Kakao Mobility taxis, games, music and webtoons.
kan: KAN is the token of BitKan, a long-running Chinese crypto platform that started as an information and community app for Bitcoin users and grew into trading services. KAN is used for fees, rewards and perks inside BitKan.
kao: Kao is a Japanese consumer goods company based in Tokyo, founded in 1887 as a soap maker. It sells household and personal care products such as Attack detergent, Bioré skin care, Merries diapers and Kanebo cosmetics, as well as industrial chemicals.
kas: Kaspa is a Proof of Work cryptocurrency launched in November 2021 with no premine or presale. It uses a BlockDAG structure (the GHOSTDAG protocol), which lets blocks be created in parallel and confirms transfers very quickly.
kat: Katana is a DeFi-focused blockchain incubated by Polygon Labs and GSR, built to concentrate liquidity for trading and lending. Holders lock KAT to receive vKAT, which gives votes on how rewards and capital are directed across the network.
kata: Katana Inu (KATA) is the token of a play-to-earn multiplayer action game with PvP and battle royale modes, played from a third-person view. KATA is used inside the game and exists on both Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain; the token launched in late 2021.
kau: Kinesis Gold (KAU) is a gold-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one gram of investment-grade gold held in insured vaults. Holders can spend, transfer or redeem it and receive a share of the platform's fees as a yield.
kava: Kava (KAVA) is a layer-1 blockchain that connects the Ethereum and Cosmos ecosystems and offers DeFi services that work like a decentralized bank, such as lending and stablecoins. KAVA is used for staking, fees and governance.
kawasaki-heavy-industries: Kawasaki Heavy Industries is a Japanese engineering group with head offices in Tokyo and Kobe, founded in 1896 as a shipyard. It builds Shinkansen trains, ships, aircraft and jet engine parts, industrial robots and gas turbines, and Kawasaki motorcycles through its subsidiary Kawasaki Motors.
kazt: KuibyshevAzot is a Russian chemical company in Togliatti, Samara region. It produces nitrogen fertilizers such as ammonia, urea and ammonium sulphate, as well as caprolactam, polyamide and technical yarns.
kb-financial: KB Financial Group is one of South Korea's largest financial groups, based in Seoul. Its core business is KB Kookmin Bank, one of the country's biggest banks, and it also runs credit cards, securities, insurance and asset-management companies serving millions of Korean customers.
kbank: Kasikornbank (KBank) is one of Thailand's largest commercial banks, based in Bangkok and founded in 1945 as Thai Farmers Bank. It serves individuals, small businesses and corporations and is known for its K PLUS mobile banking app.
kbc: KBC Group is a Belgian bank and insurance group based in Brussels. It serves retail, small-business and corporate clients in Belgium and in central Europe through ČSOB in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, K&H in Hungary and UBB in Bulgaria.
kbh: KB Home is a US homebuilder based in Los Angeles, founded in 1957 as Kaufman & Broad. It builds and sells single-family homes, townhomes and condos, mainly for first-time and move-up buyers, and lets buyers personalize homes in its design studios.
kbr: KBR is a US engineering and technology company from Houston, Texas. It provides science, engineering and IT services to governments — including NASA and the US military — and licenses process technologies for ammonia, fertilizer, refining and chemical plants. Until 2007 it was part of Halliburton.
kbsb: TNS energo Kuban is a Russian electricity retailer based in Krasnodar and part of the TNS energo group. As the supplier of last resort in Krasnodar Krai and Adygea, it buys power on the wholesale market and sells it to households and businesses.
kbx: Knorr-Bremse is a German manufacturer based in Munich, founded in 1905. It is a world leader in braking systems for trains and commercial vehicles such as trucks and buses, and also makes doors, climate control and driver-assistance systems.
kche: Kamchatskenergo is the main power and heat company of the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia's Far East, part of the RusHydro group. It runs thermal, geothermal and small hydro plants and supplies electricity and heat to Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky and the region.
kchol: Koç Holding is Turkey's largest industrial conglomerate, based in Istanbul and founded by Vehbi Koç in 1926. Its companies span energy (Tüpraş), cars (Ford Otosan, Tofaş), home appliances (Arçelik, Beko) and banking (Yapı Kredi).
kcr: Konecranes is a Finnish maker of cranes and lifting equipment based in Hyvinkää. It builds industrial overhead cranes, port cranes and container handling machines and earns much of its revenue from servicing them.
kcs: KuCoin Token (KCS) is the native token of KuCoin, an international crypto exchange founded in 2017. Holders get discounts on trading fees and a share of bonuses, and KCS also pays fees on the KCC network.
kct: Konnect (KCT) is a blockchain project that links a lifestyle membership with an e-commerce platform in a B2B2C model. Members use the KCT token for benefits across shopping, travel, tourism and cultural services from partner businesses.
kd: Kyndryl is a New York–based IT infrastructure services company spun off from IBM in 2021. It runs and modernizes data centers, cloud systems, networks and security for large companies and governments around the world.
kda: Kadena is a proof-of-work blockchain founded in 2016 by former JPMorgan engineers Stuart Popejoy and Will Martino. Its Chainweb design runs many chains in parallel to raise capacity, and it uses its own safety-focused smart-contract language, Pact. In 2025 the Kadena company announced it was winding down, while the network continues with its miners and community.
kddi: KDDI is Japan's second-largest telecom company, based in Tokyo. It provides mobile service under the au, UQ mobile and povo brands, home internet, and financial, energy and corporate IT services.
kdk: Kodiak Finance (KDK) is a decentralised exchange and liquidity platform on Berachain. It offers token swaps, automated liquidity vaults and a token launch tool; KDK is its native token.
kdp: Keurig Dr Pepper is a US beverage company based in Burlington, Massachusetts, and Frisco, Texas, formed in 2018 by merging Keurig and Dr Pepper Snapple. It sells Dr Pepper, 7UP and Canada Dry sodas plus Keurig coffee makers and K-Cup pods.
keep: Keep Network (KEEP) was an Ethereum project that stored and processed private data off-chain in 'keeps' protected by secure multi-party computation, and it created the bitcoin bridge tBTC. In 2022 it merged with NuCypher into Threshold Network, and KEEP can be swapped for the T token.
kekius: Kekius Maximus is a memecoin named after the joke name Elon Musk briefly used on his X profile at the end of 2024. The project is community-driven and has no function beyond the meme.
kemira: Kemira is a Finnish chemicals company based in Helsinki, founded in 1920. It makes chemicals for water treatment and for the pulp and paper industry, used by cities and industrial customers worldwide.
kepco: KEPCO (Korea Electric Power Corporation) is South Korea's state-controlled power company, headquartered in Naju. It is the country's sole operator of electricity transmission and distribution, and through subsidiaries it generates power at coal, gas and nuclear plants and builds nuclear plants abroad.
ker: Kernel is a Ukrainian agribusiness founded in 1995 by Andriy Verevskyi, whose shares were listed in Warsaw. It is one of the world's leading exporters of sunflower oil: it grows grain, crushes oilseeds and ships products through its own port terminals.
ker-fr: Kering is a French luxury group from Paris controlled by the Pinault family. It owns the fashion houses Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga and the jewellers Boucheron and Pomellato.
kernel: KernelDAO is an ecosystem of restaking products on Ethereum and BNB Chain: the Kelp liquid restaking protocol, Kernel infrastructure and the Gain yield vaults. The KERNEL token is used for governance and staking.
keskob: Kesko is a Finnish retail company based in Helsinki. It runs grocery stores such as K-Citymarket and K-Supermarket, building and technical trade chains in Finland and the Nordic and Baltic countries, and car sales.
kex: Kirby Corporation is a Houston company that runs the largest fleet of inland tank barges in the United States, moving petrochemicals, oil products and other liquids on rivers and coastal waters. It also services and distributes engines, transmissions and power equipment.
key: KeyCorp is a US regional banking group from Cleveland, Ohio, and the parent of KeyBank. It serves individuals and businesses in around 15 states with accounts, loans, mortgages and investment banking for mid-sized companies.
keycat: Keyboard Cat (KEYCAT) is a memecoin on Base inspired by the viral 'Keyboard Cat' video of a cat in a shirt playing a keyboard. It is a community token with no utility beyond trading.
keyence: Keyence is a Japanese industrial automation company based in Osaka, founded in 1974. It develops sensors, machine vision systems, measuring instruments and microscopes, runs without its own factories, and is known for exceptionally high profitability.
keys: Keysight Technologies is a US company from Santa Rosa, California, spun off from Agilent in 2014 and originally rooted in Hewlett-Packard. It makes oscilloscopes, analyzers and software for designing and testing electronics, 5G networks, chips and automotive systems.
kfba: Ingrad is a Russian residential property developer based in Moscow. It builds large apartment complexes in Moscow and the Moscow region, from planning and construction to sales.
kgen: KGeN is a Web3 gaming platform that builds a network of verified real players and lets game publishers reach a live audience instead of bots. The project has a strong presence in India; KGEN is the ecosystem token.
kgf: Kingfisher is a British home-improvement retailer based in London. It runs DIY and trade chains such as B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Dépôt in France and Poland, selling tools, building materials, garden and home products.
kgh: KGHM Polska Miedź is a Polish mining and metals company from Lubin and one of the world's largest producers of copper and silver. It mines ore in Lower Silesia, has mines in Chile, the US and Canada, and is controlled by the Polish state.
kgst: KGST is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Kyrgyz som and fully backed by reserves. It is designed as a digital form of the som for fast, transparent payments and transfers in Kyrgyzstan and the wider Central Asian region.
kgx: KION Group is a German maker of forklifts and warehouse technology based in Frankfurt. It builds industrial trucks under the Linde and STILL brands and, through Dematic, designs automated warehouse and supply-chain systems.
khc: Kraft Heinz is one of the largest food makers in North America, formed in 2015 by merging Kraft and Heinz with backing from Berkshire Hathaway and 3G Capital. Its brands include Heinz ketchup, Philadelphia cream cheese, Kraft Mac & Cheese, Oscar Mayer and Lunchables.
kia: Kia is a South Korean carmaker from Seoul, founded in 1944 and part of Hyundai Motor Group since 1998. It builds cars, SUVs and electric vehicles such as the EV series at plants in Korea, the US, Europe and India.
kii: KiiChain (KII) is a layer-1 blockchain built for emerging markets, especially Latin America. It focuses on stablecoin payments, currency exchange and tokenizing real-world assets for local businesses.
kim: Kimco Realty is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) from Jericho, New York, founded in 1958. It owns and operates open-air shopping centers anchored by grocery stores, mostly in major US metro areas.
kimbera: Kimberly-Clark de México is a Mexican maker of personal-care and paper products, affiliated with the US company Kimberly-Clark. It produces diapers, toilet paper, tissues and feminine care items under brands such as Huggies, Kleenex, Pétalo and Kotex.
kimchi: Aura Final Boss (KIMCHI) is a community meme token on Solana launched through pump.fun and tied to the crypto influencer kimchi1x. Its name mixes two internet slang terms, "aura" for charisma and "final boss" from gaming, and it has no use beyond community and trading.
kishu: Kishu Inu (KISHU) is a dog-themed memecoin on Ethereum launched in 2021, during the wave of coins inspired by Dogecoin and Shiba Inu. It is driven by its community and has no utility beyond trading.
kite: Kite is a blockchain for the "agentic economy", where AI agents can make payments on their own and securely. The network supports the x402 standard that lets machines pay for online services; KITE is its native token for staking and fees.
kkr: KKR & Co. is a global investment firm based in New York, founded in 1976 by Henry Kravis, George Roberts and Jerome Kohlberg. A pioneer of leveraged buyouts, it manages private equity, credit, infrastructure and real estate funds and owns the insurer Global Atlantic.
klac: KLA Corporation is an American maker of process-control equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, based in California. Its inspection and metrology systems find defects on silicon wafers and photomasks; its customers are the world's largest chipmakers.
klar: Klarna is a Swedish fintech company from Stockholm, founded in 2005 by Sebastian Siemiatkowski. Best known for buy now, pay later at online and in-store checkout, it also offers a shopping app, the Klarna Card and bank accounts in some countries.
klbf: Kalbe Farma is one of Southeast Asia's largest pharmaceutical companies, based in Jakarta and founded in 1966. It makes medicines, supplements, infant and sports nutrition; well-known brands include Promag and the energy drink Extra Joss.
klbn11: Klabin is Brazil's largest maker of packaging paper and paperboard, based in São Paulo and founded in 1899. It grows its own pine and eucalyptus plantations and produces pulp, kraft paper, corrugated boxes and paper sacks.
kled: Kled AI (KLED) is the token of Kled, a mobile app where people upload their own photos, videos and other content to be licensed as training data for AI companies, and get paid for their contributions.
klv: Klever is a crypto company founded in 2019 by a Brazilian team, known for the Klever Wallet app and its own blockchain, KleverChain. KLV is the native coin of KleverChain, used for fees, staking and governance.
kmaz: KAMAZ is Russia's largest truck maker, based in Naberezhnye Chelny in Tatarstan, with production starting in 1976. It builds heavy trucks, buses and engines and its team is famous for many Dakar Rally wins.
kmb: Kimberly-Clark is a US maker of personal care products based in Irving, Texas, founded in 1872. It sells Kleenex tissues, Huggies diapers, Cottonelle and Scott toilet paper and Kotex feminine care products worldwide.
kmd: Komodo is a blockchain project launched in 2016 as a fork of Zcash. It is known for delayed proof of work, which regularly records its blocks on the bitcoin blockchain for extra security, and for atomic-swap technology behind its non-custodial Komodo Wallet and decentralized exchange. KMD is the platform's coin.
kmi: Kinder Morgan is a US energy infrastructure company based in Houston, founded in 1997 by Richard Kinder. It owns one of North America's largest natural gas pipeline networks, as well as pipelines for refined products and storage terminals.
kmno: Kamino is a DeFi platform on Solana that combines lending, borrowing, leverage and automated liquidity management. It began as the easiest way to earn from providing liquidity through one-click, auto-compounding strategies; KMNO is the governance token.
kmx: CarMax is the largest used-car retailer in the United States, based in Richmond, Virginia, and founded in 1993. It sells cars at no-haggle prices in stores and online, buys cars from people, and offers auto loans through CarMax Auto Finance.
knc: Kyber Network Crystal (KNC) is the token of KyberSwap, a decentralized aggregator that finds the best exchange rate across many DEXs on multiple networks. Kyber Network was founded in Singapore in 2017 by Loi Luu and Victor Tran; KNC is used for governance.
knebv: Kone is a Finnish elevator and escalator company based in Espoo, founded in 1910. It makes, installs and modernises elevators, escalators and automatic doors for buildings worldwide, and earns a large share of its revenue from maintenance.
knf: Knife River is a US construction materials company based in Bismarck, North Dakota, spun off from MDU Resources in 2023. It mines crushed stone, sand and gravel, makes ready-mix concrete and asphalt, and builds roads in the western and central US.
knin: Kuehne+Nagel is a Swiss logistics company based in Schindellegi, founded in Bremen in 1890. It arranges sea and air freight, contract logistics and warehousing and is one of the world's largest freight forwarders.
knsl: Kinsale Capital is an American insurance company based in Richmond, Virginia, founded in 2009. It specialises in excess and surplus lines: insuring small businesses and unusual commercial risks that standard insurers often decline.
kntq: Kinetiq (KNTQ) is the token of a liquid staking protocol on Hyperliquid that issues kHYPE for staked HYPE. The team also builds Markets.xyz for round-the-clock futures trading on stocks, currencies and commodities.
knx: Knight-Swift Transportation is one of North America's largest trucking companies, based in Phoenix, Arizona, and formed in 2017 by the merger of Knight Transportation and Swift. It hauls full truckloads, runs less-than-truckload freight, logistics brokerage and rail-truck intermodal services in the US and Mexico.
ko: The Coca-Cola Company is an American company from Atlanta and the world's largest maker of soft drinks; the Coca-Cola drink itself was invented in 1886. It also owns Sprite, Fanta, Dasani water and Costa Coffee, and sells its products in more than 200 countries.
kofol: Kofola ČeskoSlovensko is a Czech-Slovak drinks company best known for Kofola, a herbal cola first made in Czechoslovakia in 1960. It also sells mineral waters and juices such as Rajec, Vinea and Radenska in Central Europe.
kofubl: Coca-Cola FEMSA is a Mexican company and the world's largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler by sales volume. It produces and distributes Coca-Cola drinks in Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina and other Latin American countries.
kog: Kongsberg Gruppen is a Norwegian technology and defence group based in Kongsberg, founded in 1814 as a state weapons factory and still half-owned by the Norwegian state. It makes the NASAMS air-defence system and Naval Strike Missile, plus navigation, automation and other systems for ships and offshore industries.
koge: KOGE is a token on BNB Chain issued by 48 Club, a long-running BNB Chain community that operates validators and MEV-protection infrastructure. The token is used inside the 48 Club ecosystem and is widely traded on BNB Chain exchanges.
kogk: Korshunov Mining Plant is a Russian iron ore producer in Zheleznogorsk-Ilimsky in the Irkutsk region, part of the Mechel group. It mines iron ore and makes iron ore concentrate for steel plants.
kom: Kommunitas (KOM) is a decentralized launchpad where crypto projects raise funds from the community before listing, without the usual tier system that favors large holders. It works across several blockchains, and KOM is staked to take part in token sales and governance.
