rion: Hyperion (RION) is a decentralized exchange on the Aptos blockchain that combines a swap aggregator, concentrated liquidity and automated vaults. RION is its utility token for trading incentives and rewards; staking it gives xRION for voting. The token launched in July 2025.
riot: Riot Platforms is a US bitcoin miner from Castle Rock, Colorado. It runs large mining sites in Texas, including Rockdale and Corsicana, holds bitcoin on its balance sheet and is converting part of its power capacity into data centers for AI and high-performance computing.
ritual: Ritual (RITUAL) is a project building a blockchain on which smart contracts can call AI models directly. Its Infernet network connects on-chain applications with AI computation running off-chain.
riv: RIV Coin (RIV) is a governance token on the Solana blockchain. Holders can vote on decisions about the project's development, and the token is tied to the RIV Capital community.
river: River (RIVER) is a chain-abstraction stablecoin system: users lock collateral on one blockchain and receive the satUSD stablecoin and yield on others, without bridges. RIVER is the ecosystem's token.
rivn: Rivian is a US electric-vehicle maker from Irvine, California, founded in 2009 by RJ Scaringe. It builds the R1T pickup and R1S SUV, electric delivery vans used by Amazon, and is launching the smaller R2.
riyad-bank: Riyad Bank is one of Saudi Arabia's largest banks, headquartered in Riyadh and founded in 1957. It serves corporations, government-linked projects and individual customers with loans, deposits, investment and brokerage services, and is expanding its digital banking.
riz: Rivalz Network (RIZ) is the token of Rivalz, a decentralised AI infrastructure project that runs a data, storage and compute layer for AI agents, supported by community-run node clients.
rize: RIZE is the token of T-RIZE, a platform for compliant tokenization of real-world assets. Asset owners turn projects into tokens, investors buy fractional stakes through regulated distributors, and a privacy-preserving machine-learning layer helps with due diligence and valuation.
rjf: Raymond James Financial is an American financial company from St. Petersburg, Florida, founded in 1962. It offers wealth management through a network of financial advisors, investment banking and banking products.
rkke: RKK Energia is a Russian space company based in Korolyov near Moscow, founded in 1946 by Sergei Korolev's design bureau. It builds the Soyuz crewed spacecraft and Progress cargo ships and runs the Russian segment of the International Space Station.
rklb: Rocket Lab is a space company founded in New Zealand in 2006 by Peter Beck and now headquartered in Long Beach, California. It launches small satellites with its Electron rocket, is developing the larger reusable Neutron rocket, and builds spacecraft and parts such as solar panels and reaction wheels for other missions.
rkt: Reckitt (Reckitt Benckiser) is a British consumer health and hygiene company based in Slough, with roots going back to 1840. Its well-known brands include Dettol, Lysol, Finish, Vanish, Durex, Strepsils and Nurofen, sold in nearly every country.
rl: Ralph Lauren is a New York fashion house founded in 1967 by designer Ralph Lauren. It sells clothing, accessories and home goods; its best-known symbol is the polo shirt with the logo of a player on horseback.
rlc: iExec RLC is a French decentralized computing project from Lyon, founded in 2016. It lets developers build apps that process private data inside protected environments, and the RLC token pays for computing power and data.
rli: RLI Corp. is an American specialty insurance company from Peoria, Illinois, founded in 1965. It writes niche property and casualty insurance and surety bonds for businesses, such as commercial umbrella, transportation and professional liability coverage.
rls: Rayls is a blockchain platform for banks and financial institutions, developed by the Brazilian company Parfin. It combines private networks for institutions with an EVM-compatible public chain, so tokenized assets can move while keeping data confidential. RLS is its token.
rlusd: Ripple USD (RLUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched by Ripple in December 2024. It is issued under a New York trust charter, backed by dollar deposits, short-term US Treasuries and cash equivalents, and runs on both the XRP Ledger and Ethereum, mainly for payments and institutional use.
rmbs: Rambus is an American semiconductor company from San Jose, California, founded in 1990. It designs memory interface chips for servers, security and interface IP, and licenses its patents to chipmakers, with a focus on data centres and AI.
rmd: ResMed is an American-Australian company from San Diego that makes CPAP machines and masks for treating sleep apnea and other breathing disorders. Its devices connect to the cloud, so doctors can monitor patients' therapy remotely.
rms: Hermès is a Paris-based French luxury house founded in 1837 as a harness workshop. Today it makes the iconic Birkin and Kelly bags, silk scarves, clothing, perfumes and watches; the founder's family still holds control.
rnbw: RNBW is the token of Rainbow, a popular self-custody crypto wallet app for Ethereum and its layer 2 networks, known for its colourful, beginner-friendly design. The token rewards users and gives them a say in the project.
rnft: RussNeft is a Russian oil company based in Moscow, founded in 2002 by Mikhail Gutseriev. It produces oil mainly in Western Siberia and the Volga-Urals region and sells crude and oil products.
rno: Renault is a French carmaker based in Boulogne-Billancourt near Paris, founded in 1899 by the Renault brothers. It makes Renault, budget Dacia and sporty Alpine cars, and with Nissan and Mitsubishi forms one of the world's biggest car alliances.
rnr: RenaissanceRe is a global reinsurance company based in Bermuda, founded in 1993. It is known for property catastrophe reinsurance, protecting insurers against large losses from hurricanes, earthquakes and other disasters, and also writes casualty and specialty reinsurance.
rnt: RNT is the utility token of Reental, a Spanish platform that lets people invest in real estate through blockchain tokens representing shares in properties. The token is used within Reental's platforms.
roa: ROACORE (ROA) is a Web3 ecosystem on Solana that turns everyday activity such as walking, cultural events and digital engagement into rewards. It includes the DOGDOG, MODA Gallery and ROA STORE apps, and ROA is the ecosystem's token.
roam: ROAM is a decentralized wireless (DePIN) network that aims to give users free, seamless WiFi roaming worldwide using the OpenRoaming standard. People who share hotspots or check in to networks earn rewards; ROAM is the network's token.
robo: Fabric Protocol (ROBO) is an open global network, backed by the non-profit Fabric Foundation, for building, governing and improving general-purpose robots together. A public ledger with verifiable computing coordinates the data, computation and rules that robots and the people working with them rely on.
rock-b: Rockwool is a Danish company based in Hedehusene near Copenhagen and the world's largest maker of stone wool. It turns volcanic rock into fire-resistant insulation for buildings and industry, and also makes Rockfon acoustic ceilings and Grodan growing media for greenhouses.
roiv: Roivant Sciences is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 by Vivek Ramaswamy. It builds subsidiary 'Vants' that license and develop drug candidates, mainly for immune and inflammatory diseases, and has sold successful programmes to big pharma companies.
rok: Rockwell Automation is an American industrial automation company based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, with roots going back to 1903. Through its Allen-Bradley brand and FactoryTalk software it supplies controllers, motor drives, sensors and software that run production lines in factories, from cars to food and pharmaceuticals.
roku: Roku is an American streaming platform company from San Jose, California, founded in 2002 by Anthony Wood. It makes the Roku operating system for smart TVs and streaming sticks and earns most of its money from advertising and content partnerships on its platform.
rol: Rollins is a US pest-control company based in Atlanta that owns Orkin, one of America's best-known pest-control brands, along with other services. It protects homes and businesses in many countries from termites, rodents, insects and wildlife.
roll: RollX is a decentralised trading platform native to Base that aims to offer exchange-level speed while keeping DeFi principles: transparency, self-custody and composability. ROLL is the platform's token.
rolo: Rusolovo is Russia's main tin mining company, with deposits in the Khabarovsk region of the Far East. It mines tin ore and produces tin concentrate, a key raw material for solder and electronics.
ron: Ronin (RON) is a gaming blockchain created by Vietnamese studio Sky Mavis for the game Axie Infinity. It offers cheap, fast transactions for in-game economies and NFTs, and RON is used to pay fees and for staking.
roobee: Roobee (ROOBEE) is the token of Roobee, a blockchain-based investment platform launched in 2019 for non-professional investors, offering ready-made portfolios of crypto and traditional assets with a low entry threshold.
rop: Roper Technologies is a US conglomerate from Sarasota, Florida, that grew from a pump maker into an owner of niche software companies. It buys and develops vertical software for healthcare, insurance, education, transportation and construction.
rosa: Rosa Inu (ROSA) is a meme coin. Like most meme coins, it is not backed by a business or assets, and its price is driven mainly by community attention and trading.
rose: Oasis Network (ROSE) is a layer-1 blockchain for confidential applications, founded by Berkeley professor Dawn Song. Its key network, Sapphire, is an EVM-compatible environment where smart contracts can work with private data; ROSE pays for fees and staking.
rosn: Rosneft is Russia's largest oil company, controlled by the state and based in Moscow. It produces oil and gas in Siberia, the Far East and the Arctic, runs large refineries and is under Western sanctions.
rost: Ross Stores is a US off-price retail chain based in Dublin, California. Through its Ross Dress for Less and dd's DISCOUNTS stores it sells branded clothing, shoes and home goods at discounts to regular department-store prices.
rovi: Laboratorios Rovi is a Spanish pharmaceutical company based in Madrid. It is known for low-molecular-weight heparins such as enoxaparin, develops long-acting injectable medicines, and makes injectable drugs and vaccines for other companies.
rpl: Rocket Pool (RPL) is a decentralized liquid staking protocol for Ethereum, founded in Australia. Users can stake from 0.01 ETH and receive the rETH token, while node operators lock up RPL as extra collateral that guarantees honest behaviour.
rpm: RPM International is an American coatings and sealants company from Medina, Ohio, founded in 1947. Its brands include Rust-Oleum paints, DAP caulks and sealants, Zinsser primers and Carboline industrial coatings for homes, construction and industry.
rr: Rolls-Royce Holdings is a British engineering company based in London, founded in 1906. It makes Trent engines for widebody Airbus and Boeing jets, engines for military aircraft and nuclear submarines; the Rolls-Royce car brand belongs to BMW.
rrc: Range Resources is an American natural gas producer from Fort Worth, Texas. It drills and produces natural gas and natural gas liquids from the Marcellus Shale in Pennsylvania and was a pioneer of Marcellus drilling in 2004.
rrx: Regal Rexnord is an American industrial company from Milwaukee, Wisconsin. It makes electric motors, power transmission components such as bearings, couplings and gearboxes, conveyor products and automation systems used in factories, HVAC equipment and warehouses.
rs: Reliance, Inc. (formerly Reliance Steel & Aluminum) is an American metals service center company from Scottsdale, Arizona, founded in 1939. It buys steel, aluminum and other metals in bulk, cuts and processes them and delivers small orders quickly to manufacturers.
rsc: ResearchCoin (RSC) is the token of ResearchHub, an open-science platform co-founded by Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong. It rewards scientists for publishing, peer-reviewing and discussing research.
rsg: Republic Services is the second-largest waste management company in the United States, based in Phoenix, Arizona. It collects household and business trash, sorts recyclables and runs landfills, serving millions of customers across the country.
rsgp: Cambria (RSGP) is the token of Cambria, a browser-based dark fantasy MMORPG where players put real money at risk and rewards come from game revenue rather than new token issuance. The game has run mainly on Ronin and Abstract, and RSGP is planned for governance, staking, fee discounts and cosmetics.
rsr: Reserve Rights (RSR) is the token of the Reserve protocol, where anyone can issue a stablecoin or index token backed by a basket of assets. RSR insures these tokens: it is staked as extra collateral in case the reserve loses value, and it is also used for governance.
rtkm: Rostelecom is Russia's largest provider of digital services and fixed-line telecoms, controlled by the state. It offers home internet, TV and phone service, owns mobile operator T2, and runs data centres and cloud services.
rtsb: TNS energo Rostov-on-Don is the main electricity retailer in the Rostov region of southern Russia, part of the TNS energo group. It buys power on the wholesale market and sells it to households and businesses in the region.
rtx: RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies) is a US aerospace and defense company based in Arlington, Virginia. It combines jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, avionics supplier Collins Aerospace and Raytheon, which builds missiles and Patriot air-defense systems.
rual: Rusal is a Russian aluminium company and one of the world's largest aluminium producers. Its smelters run mainly in Siberia on cheap hydropower, and it owns a large stake in Nornickel.
ruji: Rujira (RUJI) is an app layer on THORChain that brings swaps, perpetual futures, lending and liquidations together in one interface. Users work with native coins such as real Bitcoin straight from their own wallet, without third-party bridges or wrapped tokens.
run: Sunrun is a US home solar company from San Francisco, founded in 2007, and the country's largest provider of residential solar. Instead of selling panels outright, it mostly leases solar systems and home batteries to households for a monthly fee and can link them into virtual power plants.
rune: THORChain is a decentralized cross-chain exchange that lets users swap native coins between blockchains, such as real Bitcoin for ETH, without bridges or wrapped tokens. RUNE is the base asset of its liquidity pools and is bonded by node operators to secure the network.
rusi: Russ-Invest is a Russian investment company based in Moscow. It invests its own capital in shares, bonds and other financial assets and also offers brokerage and asset management services.
rvf: RocketX Exchange (RVF) is the token of RocketX, a hybrid aggregator that compares prices across many centralized and decentralized exchanges to find the best swap rate. It also offers apps a single API for in-app swaps and one-click cross-chain transfers; RVF runs on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
rvn: Ravencoin is a cryptocurrency launched in 2018 as a fork of Bitcoin, with no ICO and no premine. It specialises in issuing and transferring digital assets and is mined using the KAWPOW algorithm.
rvty: Revvity is a US life-science and diagnostics company from Waltham, Massachusetts, formed in 2023 from the former PerkinElmer's health sciences businesses. It sells lab instruments, reagents, software and newborn and disease screening tests to researchers, drugmakers and hospitals.
rwe: RWE is a German energy company from Essen, founded in 1898. It is one of the world's leaders in wind and solar power and also runs gas-fired power plants and trades energy.
rxrx: Recursion Pharmaceuticals is a US biotech company from Salt Lake City, Utah, founded in 2013. It uses automated labs, huge biological datasets and artificial intelligence to discover and develop new medicines, and in 2024 it merged with the British AI drug-discovery firm Exscientia.
ry: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is Canada's largest bank, headquartered in Toronto and founded in 1864 in Halifax. It serves individuals and businesses and runs wealth management, insurance and investment banking in Canada, the US and other countries.
rya: Ryanair is an Irish low-cost airline group from Dublin, founded in 1984 and led for decades by Michael O'Leary. It flies short-haul routes across Europe with Boeing 737 jets under the Ryanair, Buzz, Lauda and Malta Air brands.
ryan: Ryan Specialty is an American specialty insurance firm from Chicago, founded in 2010 by Patrick Ryan, who earlier built Aon. It acts as a wholesale broker and managing underwriter, placing hard-to-insure commercial risks for retail insurance brokers.
ryft: RYFT is the token of a platform on Robinhood Chain that combines an AI engine turning text prompts into playable single- and multiplayer games with a launchpad, so creators can release a token tied to each game.
rym: Ryman Healthcare is a New Zealand company based in Christchurch, founded in 1984, that builds and runs retirement villages. Its villages in New Zealand and Australia combine independent-living homes with rest-home, hospital and dementia care.
ryn: Rayonier is an American timberland real estate investment trust based in Florida, with roots going back to 1926. It owns and manages millions of acres of forests in the US South, Pacific Northwest and New Zealand, selling timber and developing land.
rzsb: Ryazanenergosbyt (Ryazan Energy Retail Company) is a Russian electricity retailer. As the region's main 'supplier of last resort', it buys power on the wholesale market and sells it to households and businesses in the Ryazan region.
s: Sonic (S) is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) layer-1 blockchain that grew out of the Fantom network, whose FTM tokens were swapped for S. It focuses on fast, cheap transactions for DeFi and gives part of the fees back to app developers.
s-etf: SentinelOne is a US cybersecurity company from Mountain View, California, founded in 2013 in Israel by Tomer Weingarten. Its AI-driven Singularity platform protects laptops, servers, cloud workloads and user identities, automatically detecting and stopping attacks such as ransomware.
s58: SATS is Singapore's main airport ground-handling and in-flight catering company, serving most airlines at Changi Airport. After buying Worldwide Flight Services in 2023 it became the world's largest air cargo handler, with operations at airports across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
s63: ST Engineering (Singapore Technologies Engineering) is a Singapore technology and engineering group. It is one of the world's largest aircraft maintenance providers, and also makes defence systems, smart-city solutions such as rail and traffic systems, and satellite communications equipment.
s68: SGX Group (Singapore Exchange) runs Singapore's stock market and one of Asia's main derivatives exchanges, formed in 1999 from the merger of the Stock Exchange of Singapore and SIMEX. Besides shares and bonds it offers widely traded futures on Asian indices, currencies and commodities.
saab-b: Saab is a Swedish defence and security company based in Stockholm, founded in 1937. It builds the Gripen fighter jet, GlobalEye surveillance aircraft, the Carl-Gustaf recoilless rifle, submarines, missiles and radar systems; it no longer has any link to Saab cars.
sab: Banco Sabadell is one of Spain's largest banks, founded in 1881 in Sabadell near Barcelona. It serves individuals and businesses in Spain and Mexico; in 2025 a hostile takeover bid by BBVA failed after too few shareholders accepted it.
sab-vn: Sabeco is Vietnam's largest brewer, based in Ho Chi Minh City and maker of Bia Saigon and 333 beers. Thailand's ThaiBev has held a controlling stake since 2017; the brewery traces its history to the late 19th century.
sabic: SABIC (Saudi Basic Industries Corporation) is one of the world's largest petrochemical companies, based in Riyadh and founded in 1976. It makes plastics such as polyethylene and polypropylene, industrial chemicals, specialty materials and, through SABIC Agri-Nutrients, fertilizers; Saudi Aramco owns 70% of it.
saf: Safran is a French aerospace and defence company based in Paris. Through CFM, its joint venture with GE, it makes the popular LEAP jet engines for the Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX, as well as landing gear, brakes, cabin interiors and navigation systems.
safe: Safe (SAFE), formerly Gnosis Safe, is the standard for multisignature wallets on Ethereum and other chains, where a transfer needs approval from several keys. DAOs, funds and companies use it to hold assets; SAFE is the ecosystem's governance token.
saga: Saga (SAGA) is a layer-1 protocol that lets developers launch their own dedicated blockchains, called Chainlets, in a few clicks — popular with games and entertainment apps. Co-founded by Rebecca Liao, it uses SAGA for staking and fees.
sago: SamaraEnergo is the main electricity retailer in the Samara region on the Volga in Russia. It buys power on the wholesale market and sells it to households and businesses across the region.
sahara: Sahara AI is a blockchain platform for decentralized AI development where anyone can build, contribute data or models and earn from it. It combines its own blockchain, a marketplace for datasets and AI agents; the SAHARA token is used for payments and governance.
sahol: Sabancı Holding is one of Turkey's largest conglomerates, based in Istanbul and founded by the Sabancı family. It controls Akbank, the energy company Enerjisa, the tire-cord maker Kordsa, cement plants and retail chains such as Carrefoursa.
saia: Saia is an American trucking company from Johns Creek, Georgia, with roots going back to 1924. It specialises in less-than-truckload (LTL) freight, carrying smaller shipments from many businesses through its network of terminals across the US.
saic: Science Applications International Corp. (SAIC) is an American technology company from Reston, Virginia. It provides IT modernisation, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and mission support services to US government agencies, especially defense, space and civilian departments.
sail: SailPoint is a US software company from Austin, Texas, founded in 2005, that specialises in identity security. Its platform lets large organisations control which employees, contractors and machines can access which systems and data, and spot risky access.
salm: SalMar is one of the world's largest farmed salmon producers, based on the island of Frøya in central Norway. It farms Atlantic salmon along the Norwegian coast and in Iceland, processes and sells it worldwide, and has pioneered large offshore fish farms such as Ocean Farm 1.
samo: Samoyedcoin (SAMO) is a dog-themed community memecoin on the Solana blockchain, launched in 2021 and named after the fluffy white Samoyed breed. It has no business behind it; its community promotes itself as an ambassador for Solana and has run events and charity campaigns.
sampo: Sampo is a Finnish insurance group from Helsinki. Through If, Topdanmark and Hastings it is one of the largest property and casualty insurers in the Nordic countries and also sells car insurance in the UK.
samsung-biologics: Samsung Biologics is a South Korean biopharmaceutical company from Incheon, founded in 2011 within the Samsung group. It is one of the world's largest contract manufacturers of biologic drugs (CDMO), producing antibodies and other biologics for drugmakers.
samsung-c-t: Samsung C&T is a South Korean company from Seoul and the de facto holding company of the Samsung group, with roots dating to 1938. It works in construction (it built the Burj Khalifa), trading, fashion and resorts (Everland) and holds stakes in Samsung Electronics and Samsung Biologics.
samsung-electro-mechanics: Samsung Electro-Mechanics is a South Korean electronic components maker based in Suwon and part of the Samsung Group, founded in 1973. It is one of the world's largest producers of multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) and also makes camera modules and chip package substrates for phones, cars and servers.
samsung-electronics: Samsung Electronics is a South Korean technology giant based in Suwon, founded in 1969. It is the world's largest maker of memory chips and a leader in Galaxy smartphones, TVs and home appliances, and it also makes chips for other companies.
samsung-life: Samsung Life Insurance is South Korea's largest life insurer, headquartered in Seoul and founded in 1957. It offers life, health, retirement and savings products and owns a stake in Samsung Electronics.
samsung-sdi: Samsung SDI is a South Korean maker of batteries and electronic materials from Yongin, part of the Samsung group. It produces batteries for electric cars, including BMW models, energy storage systems and power tools.
san: Sanofi is a French pharmaceutical company based in Paris and one of the largest in the world. It makes medicines for immunology, rare diseases and cancer, including the blockbuster Dupixent, and is one of the world's leading vaccine makers.
san-es: Banco Santander is Spain's largest bank and one of Europe's biggest, founded in 1857 in the city of Santander. It operates in Spain, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Mexico, the United States and other countries, serves well over a hundred million customers and runs a large car-finance business, Santander Consumer.
sanb11: Santander Brasil is the Brazilian subsidiary of Spain's Banco Santander and one of Brazil's largest private banks, based in São Paulo. It offers current accounts, cards, loans, payroll credit, car finance and investment services to individuals and companies; SANB11 is a unit made of its common and preferred shares.
sanc: Sanctum is liquid staking infrastructure on Solana. It lets any validator or project issue its own staked-SOL token and swap such tokens with one another instantly through a shared liquidity pool called Infinity.
sand: The Sandbox (SAND) is a virtual game world on Ethereum where players buy plots of LAND as NFTs and build games and spaces from voxel objects on them. The platform is developed with backing from Animoca Brands; SAND is used for purchases, staking and voting.
sand-se: Sandvik is a Swedish engineering group founded in 1862 in Sandviken. It makes equipment, tools and services for mining and rock excavation, and metal-cutting tools and software for manufacturing industries, under brands such as Sandvik Coromant.
sands-china: Sands China is the Hong Kong-listed Macau arm of the US casino group Las Vegas Sands. It owns and runs large integrated resorts on Macau's Cotai Strip, including The Venetian Macao, The Parisian Macao and The Londoner Macao, with casinos, hotels, shopping malls and convention space.
sanm: Sanmina is an American electronics manufacturing services company from San Jose, California, founded in 1980. It builds printed circuit board assemblies, systems and components for other companies in sectors such as communications networks, cloud, medical, defense and automotive.
santos: Santos FC Fan Token (SANTOS) is the official fan token of Santos FC, the Brazilian football club famous as Pelé's team, issued on Binance's fan token platform. Holders can vote in club polls and get access to fan rewards and experiences.
sap: SAP is a German software company based in Walldorf, founded in 1972 by former IBM engineers. Europe's largest software maker, its ERP systems such as S/4HANA run finance, purchasing and production at large companies worldwide.
sap-de: SAP is Europe's largest software company, based in Walldorf, Germany, and founded in 1972 by former IBM engineers. It builds ERP systems for managing finance, purchasing, production and staff, used by most of the world's large companies.
sapien: Sapien is an AI company building Proof of Quality (PoQ), a system for evaluating AI work: data, reasoning, answers and actions. Network participants complete and review data-labeling tasks for rewards in the SAPIEN token.
sar: Sarantis is a Greek consumer goods company based in Athens. It makes and sells cosmetics, personal-care and household products — including brands such as STR8, Carroten, Bioten and Ava — across Greece and central and eastern Europe.
saro: StandardAero is an American aerospace company from Scottsdale, Arizona and one of the largest independent providers of aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul. It services engines for airlines, business jets, helicopters and military aircraft.
sasa: SASA Polyester is a Turkish polyester maker based in Adana and part of the Erdemoğlu group. It produces polyester fibers, chips, yarns and raw materials for textiles and plastic packaging, including PET bottles.
sats: SATS (Ordinals) is a BRC-20 meme token on the Bitcoin network, named after the satoshi, the smallest unit of bitcoin. It was one of the first popular tokens issued through the Ordinals protocol.
sauce: SaucerSwap (SAUCE) is the leading decentralized exchange on the Hedera network, built from non-upgradable smart contracts with a focus on self-custody. Version 1 is a classic automated market maker and version 2 adds concentrated liquidity; Hedera's fair transaction ordering protects traders from front-running.
saudi-aramco: Saudi Aramco is Saudi Arabia's state oil company, based in Dhahran, and the world's largest oil exporter. It produces oil and gas (including at the giant Ghawar field) and owns refineries and chemical plants; part of its shares were listed in 2019.
saudi-awwal-bank: Saudi Awwal Bank (SAB) is a Saudi bank based in Riyadh, formerly known as SABB (Saudi British Bank), with HSBC as a major shareholder. It merged with Alawwal Bank in 2019 and took its current name in 2023; it is strong in corporate banking and trade finance.
saudi-electricity: Saudi Electricity Company is Saudi Arabia's main power utility, headquartered in Riyadh and formed in 2000 by merging regional electricity firms. It generates, transmits and distributes electricity to homes and businesses across the Kingdom and is largely state-owned.
saudi-national-bank: Saudi National Bank (SNB) is Saudi Arabia's largest bank, formed in 2021 by merging National Commercial Bank and Samba. Its largest shareholder is the state fund PIF, and it serves the government, corporations and millions of retail customers.
sbac: SBA Communications is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Boca Raton, Florida, founded in 1989. It owns tens of thousands of wireless towers in the Americas and beyond and leases space on them to mobile carriers for their antennas.
sbc: Stable Coin (SBC) is a payments-focused stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, issued by Brale in partnership with Stable Coin Inc. It emphasizes redeemability and regulatory compliance and comes with developer tools for gasless transactions.
sbd: Steem Dollars (SBD) is a token of the Steem blockchain, launched in 2016 for the social blogging site Steemit. It was designed to track roughly one US dollar's worth of STEEM and is paid to authors and curators as part of their rewards.
sber: Sberbank is Russia's largest bank, founded in 1841 and majority-owned by the state. It serves most of Russia's population and is building an ecosystem of digital services; it is under Western sanctions.
sbet: SharpLink Gaming is a US company that in 2025 turned from sports-betting marketing into one of the largest corporate holders of Ether (ETH). It buys and stakes ETH as its main treasury strategy, and its chairman is Joseph Lubin, a co-founder of Ethereum and founder of Consensys.
sbilife: SBI Life Insurance is one of India's largest private life insurers, based in Mumbai and controlled by State Bank of India. It sells term, savings, pension and unit-linked policies, largely through SBI's huge branch network.
sbin: State Bank of India (SBI) is India's largest bank, based in Mumbai and controlled by the state, with roots going back to 1806. It has tens of thousands of branches and offers retail, corporate, insurance and investment services to hundreds of millions of customers.
sbmo: SBM Offshore is a Dutch company based in Amsterdam that designs, builds, leases and operates floating production, storage and offloading vessels (FPSOs) for offshore oil and gas fields, especially off Brazil and Guyana.
sbo: Schoeller-Bleckmann Oilfield Equipment (SBO) is an Austrian company based in Ternitz. It makes high-precision, non-magnetic steel components and tools used in directional drilling for oil and gas and also in geothermal wells.
sbra: Sabra Health Care REIT is an American real estate investment trust from Irvine, California. It owns and leases healthcare properties such as skilled nursing facilities, senior housing and behavioral health centres in the US and Canada to care operators.
sbry: J Sainsbury is one of the UK's largest supermarket groups, founded in London in 1869 by John James and Mary Ann Sainsbury. It runs Sainsbury's supermarkets and convenience stores, the Argos general-merchandise chain and the Nectar loyalty scheme.
sbsp3: Sabesp is Brazil's largest water and sewage company, based in São Paulo and founded in 1973. It supplies drinking water and collects and treats wastewater for millions of people in hundreds of municipalities in São Paulo state; it was privatized in 2024.
sbux: Starbucks is the world's largest coffeehouse chain, founded in Seattle in 1971. It sells coffee, drinks and food in tens of thousands of cafés and coffee for home in grocery stores; Howard Schultz is famous for growing the chain.
sc: Siacoin (SC) is the token of Sia, a decentralized cloud storage network launched in 2015. Users rent disk space from independent hosts around the world, files are encrypted and spread across many nodes, and storage is paid for in SC.
sca: Scallop (SCA) is a lending and borrowing protocol on the Sui blockchain, where users deposit crypto to earn interest or take loans against collateral. SCA is its governance and reward token, and holders can lock it as veSCA for a share of protocol revenue.
scatc: Scatec is a Norwegian renewable energy company based in Oslo, founded in 2007. It develops, builds, owns and operates solar, wind, hydropower and battery storage plants, mainly in emerging markets such as South Africa, Egypt, the Philippines and Brazil, and sells the power under long-term contracts.
scb: SCB X is the Bangkok-based holding company of Siam Commercial Bank, Thailand's first Thai-owned bank, founded in 1906. Created in 2022, it groups the bank with digital lending, payments, wealth and technology businesses.
scc: Siam Cement Group (SCG) is one of Thailand's largest industrial conglomerates, founded in 1913 by royal decree of King Rama VI. It makes cement and building materials, petrochemicals through SCGC and packaging through SCGP.
schd: Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity (SCHD) holds US companies with stable and growing dividends. It is popular with people building passive income.
schg: Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth (SCHG) holds large US growth companies at a very low fee, with a heavy tilt towards technology.
schw: Charles Schwab is one of the largest US brokers and wealth managers, founded by Charles Schwab in 1971 and now headquartered in Texas. It offers commission-free stock trading, banking and retirement accounts, and it bought TD Ameritrade in 2020.
sci: Service Corporation International is an American company from Houston, founded in 1962 and the largest provider of funeral, cremation and cemetery services in North America. It operates funeral homes and cemeteries, many under the Dignity Memorial brand.
scmn: Swisscom is Switzerland's largest telecom operator, headquartered in Bern, with the state holding a controlling stake. It provides mobile, internet and TV services and also operates in Italy through its subsidiary Fastweb.
scor: Scor (SCOR) is the token of an on-chain sports engagement protocol. Fans get a permanent on-chain identity (SCOR-ID) that records their activity and skill, while licensed teams, leagues and athletes use the platform to power games, collectibles and competitions.
scr: Scroll is a layer-2 network for Ethereum built on zkEVM technology and compatible with Ethereum at the bytecode level, so apps move over without changes. It uses zero-knowledge proofs to make transactions cheaper; SCR is the governance token.
scrt: Secret Network is a privacy-focused blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK whose smart contracts can process encrypted data, so inputs and balances stay hidden from the public. It grew out of the Enigma project and uses trusted hardware for privacy; SCRT pays fees and secures the network through staking.
scs: Solcasino Token (SCS) is the token of Solcasino, an online crypto casino built around the Solana blockchain. Holders can receive a share of the platform's revenue and rewards; like all gambling, it carries a high risk of loss.
scyr: Sacyr is a Spanish infrastructure group based in Madrid. It builds and operates concessions such as motorways, hospitals and airports in Spain, Latin America and other markets, and also provides water treatment and desalination services.
sd: Stader (SD) is a liquid staking platform: users stake coins such as Ether through it and receive a token like ETHx that keeps earning staking rewards while staying usable in DeFi. Stader works on several networks, and node operators use SD as collateral; SD is also its governance token.
sd-guthrie: SD Guthrie, formerly Sime Darby Plantation, is a Malaysian company and one of the world's largest producers of certified sustainable palm oil by planted area. It grows oil palm in Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea and also refines oils and develops industrial land.
sdex: SmarDex (SDEX) is a decentralized exchange designed to reduce impermanent loss, the main risk for people who provide liquidity to trading pools. It runs on Ethereum and several other networks; SDEX is used for staking, rewards and governance.
sdt: Stake DAO (SDT) is the governance token of Stake DAO, a DeFi platform that offers liquid lockers and yield strategies for governance tokens such as Curve's CRV. Users earn rewards while keeping a tradable token, and SDT holders steer the protocol.
se: Sea Limited is a Singapore-based internet company founded in 2009 by Forrest Li. It runs Shopee, one of Southeast Asia's and Brazil's biggest online shopping apps, the Garena games business (Free Fire) and the digital finance arm Monee.
seatrium: Seatrium is a Singapore offshore and marine engineering company formed in 2023 by merging Sembcorp Marine with Keppel Offshore & Marine. It designs and builds oil and gas production vessels (FPSOs), drilling rigs, offshore wind platforms and specialised ships, and repairs and upgrades vessels.
seb-a: SEB (Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken) is a Swedish bank based in Stockholm, founded in 1856 by André Oscar Wallenberg. It is a leading Nordic bank for large companies and institutions, and also serves private customers in Sweden and the Baltic countries.
sect: Sectora (SECT) is the token of a Layer 3 blockchain designed for verifying, holding and trading tokenized real-world assets, with custody, attestation and settlement built into the network itself. SECT is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum.
seda: SEDA is a modular data network that delivers and queries any type of data for smart contracts on many blockchains, acting as a programmable oracle layer. The SEDA token is used for staking and paying for data requests.
sei: Sei is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) layer-1 blockchain that uses parallel transaction execution for high speed. The network focuses mainly on trading, DeFi and games; SEI pays for fees and staking.
seic: SEI Investments is an American financial services company from Oaks, Pennsylvania, founded in 1968 by Alfred West. It provides investment processing technology, fund administration and asset management to banks, wealth advisers, institutions and fund managers.
selg: Seligdar is a Russian mining holding from the Aldan district of Yakutia. It mines gold in Yakutia and other regions and, through its Rusolovo subsidiary, is one of Russia's main tin producers.
sem: Semapa is a Portuguese industrial holding company based in Lisbon. It controls The Navigator Company, a major paper and pulp producer, the cement maker Secil, and smaller environmental and other businesses.
sent: Sentient is an open-source AI project building a community network of open models, agents and data as an alternative to closed AI labs. Through the Sentient GRID, partners combine models and computing power, and contributors are rewarded; SENT is the token at the core of the network's economy.
sentis: SentismAI (SENTIS) is an AI project on BNB Chain that offers autonomous agents to automate crypto trading, risk management, yield optimization and DAO governance across EVM-compatible networks.
serv: OpenServ is a platform for building and running AI agents that can work together across different frameworks and tasks in one shared environment. SERV is its token, used to pay for agent services and to reward developers who build agents on the platform.
seven-i: Seven & i Holdings is a Japanese retail group from Tokyo and the owner of 7-Eleven, the world's largest convenience store chain. It runs tens of thousands of 7-Eleven stores in Japan, the United States and other countries.
sf: Stifel Financial is an American wealth management and investment banking firm from St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 1890. It serves individual investors through financial advisors and offers corporate finance, trading, research and banking services.
sfi: saffron.finance (SFI) is a DeFi protocol on Ethereum that splits yield from lending and liquidity pools into risk tranches: one tranche gets steadier returns with protection, another takes more risk for higher potential yield. SFI is its governance token.
sfin: SFI is a Russian investment holding company, formerly called Safmar Financial Investments. It owns stakes in financial businesses, above all the car and equipment leasing company Europlan and the insurer VSK.
sfm: Sprouts Farmers Market is an American grocery chain from Phoenix, Arizona, founded in 2002. Its stores focus on fresh produce, natural, organic and plant-based foods, with hundreds of locations across the US.
sfp: SafePal (SFP) is a crypto wallet with hardware, mobile and browser-extension versions, backed by Binance Labs. It lets users store, swap and buy cryptocurrencies across many blockchains; the SFP token gives discounts and access to wallet features.
sgb: Songbird (SGB) is the canary network of the Flare blockchain, launched in 2021, where new features are tested under real conditions before reaching Flare. It runs decentralized price feeds for smart contracts; SGB pays fees and is used for delegation and governance.
sge: Sage Group is a British accounting software maker based in Newcastle, founded in 1981. It sells cloud software for finance, payroll and HR to small and medium-sized businesses, including Sage Intacct.

sn74: Gittensor (SN74) is the token of subnet 74 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where participants are paid in tokens for useful AI work. Its subnet, Gittensor, rewards developers for useful contributions to open-source code repositories. Subnet tokens trade against TAO in the subnet's own pool and reward the miners and validators who do its work.
sn75: Hippius (SN75) is subnet 75 of the decentralized AI network Bittensor, providing decentralized cloud data storage. Miners are rewarded for storing files, and SN75 is the subnet's alpha token.
sn79: τaos (SN79) is the token of subnet 79 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where participants are paid in tokens for useful AI work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO in the subnet's own pool and reward the miners and validators who do its work.
sn80: OpenRoboto (SN80) is the alpha token of subnet 80 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where miners compete to provide AI services and validators score their work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO and reward the subnet's participants.
sn81: grail (SN81) is the token of subnet 81 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where participants are paid in tokens for useful AI work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO in the subnet's own pool and reward the miners and validators who do its work.
sn85: Vidaio (SN85) is the token of subnet 85 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where participants are paid in tokens for useful AI work. Its subnet, Vidaio, works on AI video processing such as upscaling and compression. Subnet tokens trade against TAO in the subnet's own pool and reward the miners and validators who do its work.
sn88: Sταking (SN88) is the alpha token of subnet 88 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where miners compete to provide AI services and validators score their work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO and reward the subnet's participants.
sn9: iota (SN9) is the alpha token of subnet 9 on Bittensor, run by Macrocosmos. The subnet trains large AI models together across many independent computers on the internet, and its alpha token rewards the miners and validators doing the work.
sn92: ReinforcedAI (SN92) is the alpha token of subnet 92 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where miners compete to provide AI services and validators score their work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO and reward the subnet's participants.
sn93: Bitcast (SN93) is the alpha token of subnet 93 on Bittensor. The subnet rewards content creators, starting with YouTube, for making videos that promote briefs from Bittensor projects, measuring real audience engagement to pay them in the alpha token.
sn97: FlameWire (SN97) is the token of subnet 97 on Bittensor, a decentralized network where participants are paid in tokens for useful AI work. Subnet tokens trade against TAO in the subnet's own pool and reward the miners and validators who do its work.
sna: Snap-on is a US maker of professional tools based in Kenosha, Wisconsin, founded in 1920. It sells wrenches, power tools, diagnostic equipment and repair software, mainly to auto mechanics, largely through its fleet of mobile tool vans.
snap: Snap Inc. is a US technology company from Santa Monica, California, best known for Snapchat, the messaging app built around disappearing photos and videos, Stories and AR lenses. It earns mostly from advertising and Snapchat+ subscriptions and also develops Spectacles AR glasses.
snc: SunContract is a Slovenian blockchain project launched in 2017 that runs an energy marketplace where households and small producers, such as owners of solar panels, can buy and sell electricity directly with each other. The SNC token gives access to the platform and its benefits.
sndk: Sandisk is a US flash memory maker from Milpitas, California, founded in 1988 and spun off again from Western Digital in 2025. It produces NAND chips, SSDs, memory cards and USB drives, including under the WD brand.
snek: Snek (SNEK) is a meme token on Cardano with a snake mascot and one of the best-known meme projects in that ecosystem. It presents itself as a currency for meme creators and relies on the activity and creativity of its community.
sngs: Surgutneftegas is a Russian oil company based in Surgut, Western Siberia. It produces oil and gas, owns the Kirishi refinery and is known for its opaque ownership structure; it is under US sanctions.
snow: Snowflake is a US cloud data company founded in 2012, with its principal office in Bozeman, Montana. Its AI Data Cloud lets businesses store, combine, share and analyse large amounts of data and build AI applications on top of Amazon, Microsoft and Google clouds.
snpad: SNPad (SNPAD) powers a DePIN advertising platform: an AI smart-TV app replaces regular commercials with personalized ads, and viewers who install it receive a large share of the ad revenue in SNPad tokens.
snps: Synopsys is a US maker of chip-design software based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 1986. Chipmakers use its electronic design automation (EDA) tools and ready-made IP blocks; in 2025 it bought engineering simulation developer Ansys.
snt: Status (SNT) is a project that combines a decentralized messenger, a crypto wallet and a Web3 browser in one app. The team is also developing Status Network on Ethereum, and SNT is used for governance.
snx: Synthetix (SNX) is a DeFi protocol founded by Australian Kain Warwick that started in 2018 as a platform for synthetic assets and now runs as a decentralized perpetual futures exchange on Ethereum. SNX holders provide collateral and govern the protocol.
snx-etf: TD SYNNEX is an American IT distribution company formed in 2021 by the merger of Tech Data and SYNNEX, with headquarters in Clearwater, Florida and Fremont, California. It buys computers, software, cloud services and devices from vendors and resells them to IT resellers worldwide.
so: Southern Company is one of the largest US energy holding companies, headquartered in Atlanta. It supplies electricity in Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi and gas in several states, and owns the Vogtle nuclear plant with its new reactors.
soda: SODAX (SODA) is a cross-chain decentralized finance platform built by the team behind the ICON blockchain. It offers swaps and lending that work across many networks, and SODA is its token.
soex: SOEX is the token of Shelters of Exiles, a role-playing game universe on Telegram powered by AI agents. It belongs to the TON ecosystem and mixes AI-driven gameplay with Web3 features such as NFTs that change as players progress and a player-shaped in-game economy.
sof: Sofina is a Belgian investment holding company from Brussels, controlled by the Boël family and dating back to 1898. It invests long-term in listed and private companies and in venture and growth funds worldwide.
sofi: SoFi Technologies is a US online bank and fintech company from San Francisco, founded in 2011 to refinance student loans. Its app now offers bank accounts, loans, investing and crypto, and it also runs Galileo, a technology platform used by other fintechs.
sofl: Softline is a Russian IT company based in Moscow, founded in 1993. It sells and implements software, cloud and cybersecurity solutions for businesses and develops its own software and hardware products.
softbank-corp: SoftBank Corp is a Japanese mobile operator based in Tokyo and a subsidiary of SoftBank Group. It provides mobile service under the SoftBank, Y!mobile and LINEMO brands, home internet and business IT, and controls LY Corporation, owner of Yahoo! Japan and LINE.
softbank-group: SoftBank Group is a Japanese investment holding company based in Tokyo, founded by Masayoshi Son in 1981. It invests in tech companies through its Vision Fund, holds a controlling stake in chip designer Arm and is putting large sums into OpenAI.
sogni: Sogni AI (SOGNI) is a decentralized network for creating AI images and art. Artists use Sogni's apps to generate pictures from text prompts, while owners of graphics cards supply the computing power and are paid in SOGNI.
soil: Soil is a regulated DeFi lending protocol that lets stablecoin holders earn returns from loans backed by real-world assets, bridging traditional finance and crypto. SOIL is the protocol's token.
sokm: Şok Marketler is a Turkish discount supermarket chain based in Istanbul and part of Yıldız Holding. It runs thousands of small neighbourhood stores across Turkey selling groceries and everyday goods, many under its own private labels.
sol: Solana is a layer-1 blockchain for smart contracts, DeFi, NFTs and memecoins, known for fast and cheap transactions. It launched in 2020; co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko is originally from Ukraine.
solb: Solvay is a Belgian chemicals company based in Brussels, founded in 1863 by Ernest Solvay. It is a major producer of soda ash and related essential chemicals such as peroxides and silica; in 2023 it spun off its specialty business as Syensqo.
solo: Solomon (SOLO) is a DeFi project building a yield-bearing dollar stablecoin that stays at $1, does not rebase and earns yield, so idle stablecoin capital in swaps and perpetual exchanges becomes productive.
sols: Solstice Advanced Materials is an American specialty materials company from Morris Plains, New Jersey, spun off from Honeywell in 2025. It makes low-global-warming Solstice refrigerants, Spectra high-strength fibres, Aclar films for pharmaceutical packaging and other specialty chemicals.
solv: Solventum is a US healthcare company from St. Paul, Minnesota, spun off from 3M in 2024. It makes wound-care and infection-prevention products, dental materials, water and air filtration products and health information software.
solv-token: Solv Protocol (SOLV) is a Bitcoin staking platform that issues SolvBTC, a tokenized BTC that can be used in DeFi across many networks to earn yield. SOLV is the protocol's governance token.
somi: Somnia is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain designed for games, social networks and real-time applications. The network claims very high throughput and fees below one cent; SOMI is used to pay for transactions and for staking.
sompo-holdings: Sompo Holdings is a Tokyo-based insurance group whose core business is Sompo Japan, one of the country's biggest property and casualty insurers. It also sells life insurance, runs nursing-care homes in Japan and owns Sompo International, a global commercial insurer.
son: Sonoco Products is an American packaging company from Hartsville, South Carolina, founded in 1899. It makes metal food cans, aerosol cans, paper tubes and cores, composite cans and other industrial and consumer packaging.
son-pt: Sonae is a Portuguese conglomerate based in Maia, founded in 1959. It owns Continente, Portugal's leading supermarket chain, the electronics retailer Worten and other businesses in retail, real estate, telecoms and financial services.
sonic: Sonic SVM (SONIC) is a gaming-focused network built as an extension of Solana using the Solana Virtual Machine, developed by Mirror World. It gives games fast, cheap transactions; SONIC is used for fees, staking and governance.
sony-group: Sony Group is a Japanese conglomerate based in Tokyo, founded in 1946. It makes PlayStation consoles, camera image sensors, TVs and audio gear, and owns Sony Pictures, Sony Music and a financial services business.
soon: SOON is a stack for launching layer-2 networks based on the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) on top of different blockchains. Its Decoupled SVM design lets fast rollups with fraud proofs run on any layer 1; the project also launched a bridge between Solana and TON with a Telegram mini app.
soph: Sophon is an entertainment platform and modular network built on zkSync's ZK Stack, focused on games and consumer apps. Its goal is to bring new users into crypto through familiar products; SOPH is the network token.
soso: SoSoValue (SOSO) is an AI-powered crypto market research platform, best known for its summary data such as flows into bitcoin ETFs. It also runs the SSI protocol for index baskets of crypto assets; SOSO is used for rewards and governance.
soul: Phantasma Phoenix (SOUL) is the main token of Phantasma, a layer-1 blockchain focused on games and NFTs that has run its mainnet since 2019. It is known for smart NFTs whose properties can change over time and for tools aimed at Unity game developers, and SOUL is staked to secure the network.
soun: SoundHound AI is a US voice-AI company from Santa Clara, California, founded in 2005. Its conversational voice assistants and AI agents are used by carmakers, restaurants for phone and drive-thru ordering, TV makers and customer-service centers.
soxx: iShares Semiconductor (SOXX) is a BlackRock ETF that invests in US-listed semiconductor companies: chip designers, manufacturers and equipment makers.
soybeans: Soybeans are a major source of plant protein and oil, used for animal feed, soybean oil and tofu. Brazil and the US are the largest producers and China the largest buyer.
soyoil: Soybean oil is one of the world's most widely used cooking oils and also a feedstock for biodiesel, so its price depends on energy policy as well as food demand.
spa: Sperax is a DeFi project on Arbitrum best known for USDs, a dollar stablecoin that automatically passes yield from its collateral to holders. SPA is the governance and staking token; staked SPA (veSPA) gives voting power and rewards.
space: Spacecoin (SPACE) is a satellite-based decentralized internet project building a constellation of small low-orbit satellites to give people worldwide network access without middlemen. The SPACE token is used for payments and incentives in the network.
sparklet: Sparklet (SPARKLET) is a token from Upland, a metaverse game in which players buy, sell and develop virtual properties mapped to real-world addresses in cities around the globe. The token extends Upland's in-game economy to open crypto markets.
spbe: SPB Exchange is a Russian stock exchange based in St Petersburg, long known as the main venue for Russians to trade US and other foreign shares. Since 2023 it has been under US sanctions and has shifted to Asian and Russian securities.
spcm: SpaceM is a participation protocol on Avalanche that opens real-world projects to on-chain participation, coordinated through smart contracts. SPCM is the ecosystem's native token, used to take part in projects and for staking.
spcx: SpaceX • Robinhood Token (SPCX) is a tokenized instrument from Robinhood that tracks the value of SpaceX, Elon Musk's company that builds Falcon rockets and runs Starlink satellite internet. Robinhood issues such tokens for EU customers on the Arbitrum network.
spectre: Spectre AI (SPECTRE) is the token of an AI-powered tool that uses predictive models to help traders and investors analyse crypto markets.
spell: Spell (SPELL) is the token of Abracadabra.money, a DeFi lending protocol where users deposit interest-bearing crypto as collateral and borrow the MIM (Magic Internet Money) stablecoin. SPELL holders can stake it and vote on protocol decisions.
spg: Simon Property Group is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Indianapolis and the largest owner of shopping malls in the United States. It owns and runs malls, Premium Outlets and Mills centers, and has stakes in retailers and malls abroad.
spgi: S&P Global is a US financial information company based in New York. It owns the credit rating agency S&P Global Ratings, a stake in S&P Dow Jones Indices — the maker of the S&P 500 and Dow Jones indexes — and market data and analytics services.
spk: Spark (SPK) is an on-chain capital allocator in the Sky ecosystem (formerly MakerDAO) that deploys stablecoin reserves into DeFi, CeFi and real-world assets. Its products, such as sUSDS and sUSDC, give users yield; SPK is the governance and staking token.
spk-nz: Spark New Zealand is the country's largest telecommunications company, known as Telecom New Zealand until 2014. It provides mobile, broadband and landline services to households and businesses, along with cloud, IT and data-centre services for companies and government.
spld: Splendor (SPLD) is the token of Splendor Labs, a Layer 1 blockchain project that says it uses GPU acceleration to handle very high transaction volumes and instant micropayments for AI services, models and agents.
spot: Spotify is the world's most popular audio streaming service, founded in Stockholm, Sweden, in 2006 by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon. It offers music, podcasts and audiobooks through a free ad-supported tier and paid Premium subscriptions.
sps: Splintershards (SPS) is the governance token of Splinterlands, a blockchain trading-card game running since 2018 where players own their cards as NFTs. SPS is earned by playing and staking and lets holders vote on the game's development.
spsc: SPS Commerce is a US software company from Minneapolis, Minnesota, founded in 1987. Its cloud network connects retailers, grocers, distributors and suppliers so they can exchange orders, invoices and shipping data electronically (EDI) and share sales and inventory information.
spurs: Tottenham Hotspur FC Fan Token (SPURS) is the official fan token of the English football club Tottenham Hotspur, issued on the Socios.com platform on the Chiliz blockchain. Holders can vote in club polls and get access to fan rewards and experiences.
spx: SPX6900 is a meme coin that ironically parodies the S&P 500 stock index and traditional finance culture. It has no real technological function and is a community joke about "beating" the stock index; the token exists on Ethereum and other networks.
spxc: SPX Technologies is an American industrial company from Charlotte, North Carolina. It makes HVAC equipment such as cooling towers, boilers and heating products, plus detection and measurement gear for pipelines, utilities and transport systems.
spy: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY), launched in 1993, is the oldest US-listed ETF and tracks the S&P 500 index of 500 leading American companies — often treated as 'the market' itself.
spy-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), the oldest and one of the largest US funds following the S&P 500 index of 500 big American companies. Robinhood offers such tokens to customers in the European Union.
sqd: SQD (formerly Subsquid) is a decentralized data network that indexes blockchains and gives developers fast access to historical on-chain data. It supports hundreds of networks, and SQD is used to pay for queries and to stake nodes.
sqgrow: SquidGrow (SQGROW) is a meme token on BNB Smart Chain launched in 2022 and promoted by the pseudonymous figure "Shibtoshi". Around the token the team has built community products such as games, NFTs and staking.
sqm-b: SQM (Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile) is a Santiago-based chemical and mining company and one of the world's largest lithium producers. From the brines of the Salar de Atacama and nitrate ores in northern Chile it also makes specialty plant fertilisers, iodine and industrial salts.
sr: Spire is an American natural gas utility from St. Louis, Missouri, with roots going back to 1857. It delivers natural gas to homes and businesses in Missouri, Alabama and Mississippi and also runs gas pipelines and storage.
sre: Sempra is a US energy holding company from San Diego. It owns the California utilities SDG&E and SoCalGas, Texas's largest power grid Oncor and is developing liquefied natural gas exports.
sren: Swiss Re is a Swiss reinsurer from Zurich, founded in 1863. It insures insurance companies themselves against large risks such as natural disasters, pandemics and major accidents, and is one of the world's largest reinsurers.
srg: Snam is an Italian energy infrastructure company based in San Donato Milanese. It runs one of Europe's largest gas pipeline networks and Italy's gas storage sites, operates LNG regasification terminals and is preparing its grid to carry hydrogen.
srm: Serum (SRM) is the token of Serum, an order-book decentralized exchange on Solana launched in 2020 by FTX and Alameda Research. After the FTX collapse in 2022, the community forked Serum's code into OpenBook.
srpt: Sarepta Therapeutics is a US biotech company from Cambridge, Massachusetts, focused on genetic medicines for rare diseases. It is best known for treatments for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, including several RNA-based drugs and the gene therapy Elevidys developed with Roche.
srt3: Sartorius is a German life-science equipment maker based in Göttingen, founded in 1870. It supplies bioreactors, filters, lab balances and other tools that drug companies and labs use to develop and produce biological medicines.
srx: StorX (SRX) is a decentralized cloud storage service: files are encrypted, split into pieces and spread across nodes around the world. Node operators earn SRX for the space they provide, and the project runs on the XDC network.
ssb: SouthState is an American regional bank based in Winter Haven, Florida, with roots in South Carolina going back to 1933. It offers consumer and business banking, mortgages, wealth management and correspondent banking across the Southeast and Southwest of the US.
ssd: Simpson Manufacturing is an American building products company from Pleasanton, California, founded in 1956. Best known for Strong-Tie wood and steel connectors, it makes fasteners, anchors and structural products that help buildings resist earthquakes and high winds.
sse: SSE is a British energy company based in Perth, Scotland. It builds and runs wind farms, including the offshore Dogger Bank, hydroelectric plants in Scotland, and electricity networks in northern Scotland and southern England.
ssv: SSV Network (SSV) is decentralized infrastructure for Ethereum staking that splits the work of one validator across several independent operators. This makes staking more reliable and secure; operators are paid in SSV tokens.
st: Sensata Technologies is a sensor and electrical protection company headquartered in Attleboro, Massachusetts, which began as part of Texas Instruments. It makes pressure, temperature and position sensors, controls and circuit protection used in cars, trucks, HVAC, aerospace and industrial equipment.
st-token: Sentio Token (ST) is the token of Sentio, which builds data infrastructure for crypto developers: indexing, monitoring and analytics tools for smart contracts. ST trades on BNB Smart Chain.
stable: Stable is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for the USDT stablecoin: network fees are paid directly in USDT rather than in a volatile token. It targets payments, cross-border transfers and businesses; STABLE is the network's token for governance and staking.
stag: STAG Industrial is an American real estate investment trust from Boston, founded in 2010. It owns and leases single-tenant industrial buildings — mainly warehouses and distribution centres — across the United States.
stan: Standard Chartered is a British bank headquartered in London that earns most of its income in Asia, Africa and the Middle East. It specialises in international trade, corporate banking and wealth management, with large businesses in Hong Kong and Singapore.
standard: STANDARD is the token of Standard Reserve, a decentralized finance (DeFi) project on Robinhood Chain, the blockchain network launched by the brokerage Robinhood.
star: Starpower is a decentralized energy network (DePIN) that links home batteries, solar panels, smart plugs and electric cars into a virtual power plant. Participants earn STAR tokens for giving flexible capacity to the grid during peak hours.
stb: Storebrand is a Norwegian financial group based in Oslo, founded in 1767. It focuses on pensions, life insurance, savings and asset management in Norway and Sweden, and is known as one of the Nordic leaders in sustainable investing.
stbl: STBL is the token of a decentralized, non-custodial platform for minting stablecoins backed by real-world assets. Its USST and YLD stablecoins are designed to pass on yield from the underlying assets without staking or lock-ups.
stc: stc (Saudi Telecom Company) is Saudi Arabia's largest telecom operator, based in Riyadh. It provides mobile, home internet, cloud and cybersecurity services, also operates in Kuwait and Bahrain, and is controlled by the Public Investment Fund (PIF).
ste: STERIS is a medical technology company registered in Ireland with its main base in Ohio. It makes equipment and supplies for sterilisation and disinfection, surgical tables and lights, and provides sterilisation services for medical devices.
steem: Steem is a blockchain launched in 2016 that rewards users with tokens for posting and voting on useful content. The Steemit social network runs on it; in 2020, after a conflict with the community, the Hive blockchain split off from Steem.
sterv: Stora Enso is a Finnish-Swedish forest products company based in Helsinki and Stockholm. It makes packaging board and materials, pulp and wood products such as timber and building elements, and is one of the world's largest private forest owners.
stg: Stargate Finance is a cross-chain bridge built on LayerZero that lets users move native assets such as USDC and ETH between blockchains from unified liquidity pools with instant finality. STG is its token for governance and liquidity rewards.
stlam: Stellantis is a carmaker registered in the Netherlands, formed in 2021 by the merger of Fiat Chrysler and France's PSA Group. It owns Peugeot, Citroën, Opel, Fiat, Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Alfa Romeo and Maserati; its biggest shareholders are Exor and the Peugeot family.
stld: Steel Dynamics is one of the largest steelmakers in the United States, headquartered in Fort Wayne, Indiana. It makes steel in electric arc furnaces, recycles scrap metal and is building up aluminum production.
stmn: Straumann is a Swiss dental company from Basel, founded in 1954 and a global leader in dental implants. It also makes ClearCorrect clear aligners, biomaterials and digital tools for dentists, selling in more than 100 countries.
stmpa: STMicroelectronics is a European chipmaker headquartered in Geneva and formed in 1987 from the merger of Italy's SGS Microelettronica and France's Thomson Semiconducteurs. It makes chips for cars, industrial equipment, smartphones and computers — including STM32 microcontrollers, sensors and silicon-carbide power chips for electric vehicles.
sto: Santos is an Australian oil and gas producer based in Adelaide, founded in 1954. It produces natural gas, oil and LNG from fields in Australia and Papua New Guinea, including the Cooper Basin, and sells much of its gas to buyers in Asia.
sto-token: StakeStone (STO) is the token of StakeStone, an omnichain liquidity and yield protocol. Users deposit ETH or bitcoin and receive liquid tokens such as STONE that earn staking and strategy yield and can be used across many blockchains.
stonk: STONK is the token of stonk.fun, a launchpad on Solana where anyone can create and trade new tokens; several meme coins on the platform were launched through it.
stonkbroker: StonkBroker (STONKBROKER) is a token on Robinhood Chain, the blockchain network of the brokerage Robinhood, tied to a DeFi project that offers a token exchange (automated market maker) and a launchpad for new tokens.
storj: Storj is decentralised cloud storage: files are encrypted, split into pieces and stored on the drives of thousands of independent operators around the world. People who rent out spare disk space are paid in STORJ, and the service is compatible with Amazon S3.
storm: Storm Trade (STORM) is the token of Storm Trade, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange on The Open Network (TON) that people can use directly inside Telegram. Traders open leveraged positions on crypto and other markets, and STORM is used for staking and governance.
str: Strabag is an Austrian construction group from Vienna and one of Europe's largest builders. It builds roads, tunnels, bridges, railways, buildings and industrial facilities, mainly in Austria, Germany and Central and Eastern Europe.
strax: Xertra (STRAX) is the new name of the Stratis blockchain platform, founded in the UK in 2016. It is aimed at businesses and lets developers write smart contracts in C# on the .NET platform; STRAX is the network's native coin.
stream: Streamflow (STREAM) is the token of Streamflow, a token distribution platform on Solana. Projects use it for token vesting, airdrops, staking programs and streaming payments such as payroll, and STREAM is used for governance and fee sharing.
strk: Starknet is an Ethereum layer-2 network from the Israeli company StarkWare that uses ZK-STARK cryptographic proofs to make transactions cheaper and faster. Smart contracts are written in the Cairo language; STRK is used for fees, staking and governance.
strkbtc: strkBTC is a token that represents Bitcoin on Starknet, an Ethereum layer-2 network. It lets holders use BTC in Starknet apps — trading, lending and other DeFi — without leaving the network.
strl: Sterling Infrastructure is an American construction company from The Woodlands, Texas. It prepares large sites for data centres, factories and warehouses, builds highways, bridges and airports, and constructs residential foundations.
strs: Strauss Group is one of Israel's largest food and drink companies, based in Petah Tikva. It makes dairy products, snacks and Elite chocolate and coffee for the Israeli market, and runs a large coffee business abroad, notably the Três Corações joint venture in Brazil.
stt: State Street is a US financial company from Boston, founded in 1792. It is one of the world's largest custodian banks, and through State Street Global Advisors it runs the SPDR funds, including SPY, the oldest S&P 500 ETF.
stwd: Starwood Property Trust is an American real estate investment trust from Miami Beach, Florida, founded in 2009 and led by Barry Sternlicht. It mainly makes and buys commercial real estate loans and also invests in infrastructure lending and properties.
stx: Seagate Technology is one of the leading hard drive makers, registered in Ireland with headquarters in Cupertino, California, and founded in 1979. It produces high-capacity HDDs for data centers and the cloud, plus drives for PCs and video surveillance.
stx-token: Stacks is a network that adds smart contracts and decentralized apps to Bitcoin, relying on the security of the Bitcoin blockchain. It was founded by Muneeb Ali; STX pays network fees and powers Stacking, which earns rewards in BTC.
stz: Constellation Brands is a US drinks company from New York state. It is the exclusive US importer of Mexican beers Corona, Modelo and Pacifico, and also produces wine and spirits.
su: Schneider Electric is a French company from Rueil-Malmaison and a global leader in electrical equipment and industrial automation. It makes switchboards, energy-management systems, APC uninterruptible power supplies and data-centre equipment; its history goes back to 1836.
su-ca: Suncor Energy is an integrated Canadian oil company based in Calgary. It produces oil from the Alberta oil sands, refines it into fuel at its own refineries and sells it through the Petro-Canada chain of gas stations.
subc: Subsea 7 is an offshore engineering and construction company listed in Oslo. It designs, builds and installs seabed pipelines, risers and other subsea infrastructure for oil and gas fields, and installs foundations and cables for offshore wind farms, using its own fleet of specialised vessels.
sugar: Sugar is made from sugar cane and sugar beet. Brazil is the largest exporter and turns part of its cane into ethanol, so the sugar price is linked to oil too.
sui: Sui is a layer-1 blockchain from Mysten Labs, founded by former engineers of Meta's Diem blockchain project. It uses the Move programming language and parallel transaction processing for games, DeFi and payments.
sui-etf: Sun Communities is an American real estate investment trust from Southfield, Michigan, founded in 1975. It owns and operates manufactured housing communities and RV resorts in the US, Canada and, through Park Holidays, holiday parks in the UK.
suku: SUKU is a Web3 project that began in 2017 as a blockchain platform for supply-chain transparency and later shifted to tools that make crypto easier for newcomers, such as simple wallets and NFT creation. The SUKU token is an Ethereum-based token used across its products.
sum: Summerset is a New Zealand retirement village company founded in 1997 that builds and runs villages for older people in New Zealand and, more recently, Australia. Its villages offer independent homes, serviced apartments, rest-home and hospital care, and memory care for residents with dementia.
sumitomo-corporation: Sumitomo Corporation is one of Japan's big general trading houses, based in Tokyo and part of the Sumitomo group. It trades and invests in steel and metals, mineral resources, cars and transport, infrastructure and power, real estate and media, including the cable TV operator J:COM.
sumitomo-mitsui-fg: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) is one of Japan's three largest banking groups, based in Tokyo. Through SMBC bank it provides retail, corporate and investment banking, leasing, credit cards and brokerage in Japan and across Asia.
sun: Suncorp Group is an Australian insurer based in Brisbane. It sells home, car, business and other general insurance in Australia and New Zealand under brands such as AAMI, GIO, Suncorp, Apia and Vero, after selling its banking arm to ANZ in 2024.
sun-hung-kai-properties: Sun Hung Kai Properties is one of Hong Kong's largest property developers, founded in 1972 and controlled by the Kwok family. It builds and rents out homes, offices, shopping malls and hotels in Hong Kong and mainland China, and owns landmarks such as the International Commerce Centre, Hong Kong's tallest building.
sundog: SUNDOG is a meme token on the TRON blockchain with a dog mascot. It became TRON's best-known meme coin after Justin Sun launched the SunPump meme-token platform in 2024, and it has no real use beyond community and trading.
sunpharma: Sun Pharmaceutical is India's largest drugmaker, based in Mumbai and founded by Dilip Shanghvi in 1983. It makes generic and specialty medicines for dermatology and oncology and sells them in India, the US and other countries.
super: SuperVerse (SUPER), formerly SuperFarm, is a Web3 ecosystem that combines games, DeFi and AI tools. The SUPER token is used for transactions, staking, voting and access to the ecosystem's games and liquidity services across several blockchains.
supra: Supra (SUPRA) is a layer-1 blockchain with built-in services that usually come from outside providers: oracle price feeds, verifiable randomness and cross-chain messaging. Founded by Joshua Tobkin, it uses SUPRA for fees and staking.
supv: Grupo Supervielle is an Argentine financial group based in Buenos Aires whose core is Banco Supervielle, founded in 1887. It offers banking to individuals and companies, consumer finance, insurance, asset management and online investing through the broker IOL invertironline.
surplus: Surplus Intelligence (SURPLUS) is a marketplace for AI inference on the Base network: providers sell their unused computing capacity, and buyers such as AI agents and coding tools pay market prices to run models.
sushi: Sushi (SUSHI) is the token of SushiSwap, a decentralized exchange that appeared in 2020 as a fork of Uniswap and now runs on dozens of blockchains. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity in return for a share of trading fees; SUSHI is the governance token.
suzb3: Suzano is a Brazilian company headquartered in Salvador and São Paulo and the world's largest producer of eucalyptus pulp. It grows its own eucalyptus plantations and makes pulp, paper, paperboard and tissue, exporting to dozens of countries.
suzlon: Suzlon Energy is an Indian wind-energy company from Pune, founded in 1995 by Tulsi Tanti. It designs, manufactures and installs wind turbines and maintains wind farms, mainly in India, making it one of the country's largest wind-turbine suppliers.
suzuki-motor: Suzuki Motor is a Japanese maker of small cars and motorcycles based in Hamamatsu, founded in 1909 as a loom manufacturer. Its biggest market is India, where its subsidiary Maruti Suzuki is the leading carmaker; it also builds outboard motors.
